descripcion: The starting point of the Academia Seúl ladder: in 8 weeks you learn to read the complete Korean alphabet and to say your first real sentences about yourself, your family, your home, your day and what you like, following the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1. Reading drills live in the Hangul Reader as homework with native audio, so the live hour is reserved for speaking and being corrected. It replaces the July 2026 Level 1 and leads directly into Basic 2 (A1.2).
perfil_alumno: Spanish-speaking adults and young people from Latin America and Spain starting from absolute zero, or who recognize a few letters and words from K-pop and K-dramas but still can't read with confidence or put a sentence together. Also those who took the July Level 1 without completing the reading portion and would rather consolidate before moving up to Basic 2 (A1.2). Groups of up to 15 people, camera on and willing to make mistakes out loud.
requisito_entrada: None: the course starts from absolute zero, with no need to read Hangul or know a single word. You'll need a stable Zoom connection with camera and microphone, a notebook and pencil to trace the alphabet by hand, and to open the Hangul Reader (academiaseul.com/lector-hangul, free and no account needed) on your phone or computer before class 1.
objetivos: Read aloud any Korean syllable, including those ending in 받침 (final consonant), and write your name and the course words in Hangul
Greet, say goodbye and introduce yourself with your name and country using 저는 N이에요/예요 (I am N), choosing the right form depending on whether there is a final consonant
Ask and answer what an object is (이게 뭐예요?) and who a person is (누구예요?), and introduce your family with a photo

Count from 1 to 100 with Sino-Korean numbers and say how many people are in your family with 명 and the first native numbers (한 명, 두 명… 다섯 명); age, telling time and dates are completed in Basic 2 (A1.2)
Say where you live and where things are with N에 있어요/없어요 and position words
Talk about where you go and what you do every day with the present tense -아요/어요 and the particles 이/가 and 을/를, and say what you like with 좋아해요
Give a 1-to-2-minute oral mini-presentation about yourself without reading, understandable to a Korean speaker who talks slowly

estructura_clase.detalle: 5 items in the chat or on screen about the last session (reading, vocabulary or a structure); the worksheet and the Hangul Reader stars are checked and homework questions are answered.
The teacher presents the lesson's grammar and vocabulary from the textbook with the deck: pictures, gestures, examples using the group's real names and choral repetition before any long explanation.
Short transformation and fill-in drills (이에요/예요, particles, -아요/어요), reading aloud in turns and one-on-one pronunciation correction with cameras on.
Zoom breakout rooms with role play, dictation or a mini-dialogue from the lesson; the teacher rotates through the rooms, corrects on the spot and notes common errors for the wrap-up.
Correction of the 2 or 3 most repeated errors, the 3 key sentences of the class repeated in chorus, and assignment of the Hangul Reader, the lesson worksheet and the week's audio.

semanas.leccion: 가나다라 I (Hangul, part 1) from the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1
semanas.objetivo: Read your first syllables aloud by combining the basic vowels with the simple consonants, and understand how a Korean syllable block is built.
gramatica: Simple vowels ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ + ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ (10 vowels): shape, sound and stroke order
Simple consonants ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅊ ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅎ (14): the silent ㅇ at the start of a syllable
The consonant + vowel syllable block: the vowel goes to the right (가, 너) or underneath (고, 누); it is read left to right and top to bottom
practica: Chorus and echo: the teacher shows each vowel with her mouth and hand, everyone repeats in chorus and then one by one with cameras on (1:1 correction of ㅡ and ㅓ, the two sounds that don't exist in Spanish).
Syllable factory in pairs: in Zoom breakout rooms, one student dictates a consonant and a vowel, the other writes the syllable in the chat and reads it aloud; then they switch roles.

Lightning reading: 12 words from the textbook on screen with a picture; each student reads one aloud and the group guesses the meaning. The classroom commands 따라 하세요 (repeat after me), 읽으세요 (read) and 잘했어요 (well done) are learned by ear from day one.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Alphabet: tap and listen to the 21 vowels and 19 consonants; then Practice → Vowels and Consonants until you reach 3 stars in Reading and Listening modes.
가나다라 I worksheet: trace the 10 vowels and the 14 consonants (5 times each) and write your name in Hangul using the chart from the deck.
A 30-second audio reading the 12 words of the week, posted in the course community before class 2.
semanas.cultura: Hangul was created by King 세종 (Sejong) in 1443 so that anyone could learn to read in a day; the consonants depict the position of the tongue and lips when pronouncing them.

semanas.leccion: 가나다라 II (Hangul, part 2) + Lesson 1 안녕하세요? (Hello?) from the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1
semanas.objetivo: Read any Korean syllable, including those ending in a consonant and compound vowels, and introduce yourself with your name and country.
gramatica: 받침 (final consonant): the 7 representative pronunciations ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅇ in words like 한국 (Korea), 김치 (kimchi), 밥 (cooked rice)
Double consonants ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ and frequently used compound vowels ㅐ ㅔ ㅖ ㅚ ㅟ ㅘ ㅝ ㅢ (the ones found in 시계, 회사, 위, 의자)
저는 N이에요/예요 (I am N): 이에요 after a final consonant, 예요 after a vowel
은/는 (topic particle) only in its use for introductions: 저는 (as for me)
vocabulario: 안녕히 가세요 (goodbye, to the person leaving)
안녕히 계세요 (goodbye, to the person staying)
practica: Batchim dictation: the teacher says 10 words (한국, 김치, 밥, 선생님…), students write them in the chat and compare; final ㄹ and the difference between final ㄴ and ㅇ are corrected.
Round of introductions on camera: 안녕하세요, 저는 ___예요/이에요. 저는 ___ 사람이에요; each student listens to the previous one and repeats their name and country before introducing themselves.
Role play in pairs: meeting and parting, choosing correctly between 안녕히 가세요 and 안녕히 계세요 depending on who leaves and who stays.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice: Aspirated and tense, Syllables and Batchim until 3 stars in Reading and Listening.
Lesson 1 worksheet: complete 8 introductions with 이에요/예요 and write your own with name, country and occupation.
A 20-second audio with your full introduction, without reading, in the course community.
semanas.cultura: When greeting, Koreans bow their head (목례, a nod greeting); with an older person or a teacher the bow is deeper and always goes with the full 안녕하세요, never the 안녕 (hi, informal) heard among friends.

semanas.leccion: Lesson 2 이게 뭐예요? (What is this?) and Lesson 3 네, 빵이에요 (Yes, it's bread) from the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1
semanas.objetivo: Ask and answer what any object around you is, and affirm or deny with 네/아니요.
gramatica: 이거/그거/저거 (this/that/that over there) depending on the distance between speaker and listener; 이게 = 이거 + 가 (subject form): 이게 뭐예요?
N이에요/예요? (is it N?) and 뭐예요? (what is it?) with rising intonation
네 / 아니요 (yes / no) and the negation N이/가 아니에요 (it is not N)
practica: Show and ask: each student brings a real object up to the camera; the group asks 이게 뭐예요? and they answer 책이에요 or 아니요, 우산이에요.
Distance battle in pairs: with two objects on screen, one points using 이거/그거/저거 and the other corrects the choice depending on where each thing is relative to the two of them.
Lightning quiz with the textbook pictures: 10 images with a statement (빵이에요?), answered in chorus with 네 or 아니요 + the correct name.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Words (Reading and Listening modes) and Pictograms until 3 stars.
Written quiz on lessons 2–3 (10 items on the worksheet) + a photo of 5 objects from your home labeled in Hangul.
A 30-second audio: 5 questions and answers 이게 뭐예요? — 책이에요, recorded with the object in hand.
semanas.cultura: In Korea, 빵 (bread) is more of a bakery treat than a side to a meal: chains like 파리바게뜨 (Paris Baguette) are on almost every corner in Seoul.

semanas.leccion: Lesson 4 우리 엄마예요 (It's my mom) from the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1
semanas.objetivo: Introduce your family with a photo, ask who someone is and count from 1 to 100 with Sino-Korean numbers.
gramatica: 우리 N (our → my) for family and what's yours: 우리 엄마 (my mom), 우리 집 (my house), 우리나라 (my country)
누구예요? (who is it?) and its answer N이에요/예요; 이 사람은 (this person) to point at someone in a photo
Sino-Korean numbers 일, 이, 삼, 사, 오, 육, 칠, 팔, 구, 십, 백 (1–100): built as blocks (십오, 이십, 삼십일) and used for phone numbers, with 공 (zero)
First contact with native numbers 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷, 다섯 → 한/두/세/네/다섯 명 only to say how many people are in your family (우리 가족은 네 명이에요); the full system, age (살) and telling time (시) are covered in Basic 2
vocabulario: 언니 (older sister, said by a woman)
누나 (older sister, said by a man)
오빠 (older brother, said by a woman)
형 (older brother, said by a man)
practica: Live album: each student shares a family photo and presents it (우리 가족이에요. 이 사람은 우리 엄마예요…); the group asks 누구예요? pointing at someone else in the photo.
Sino-Korean number bingo: the teacher calls out 15 numbers between 1 and 100 and students mark their cards; in the second round the students do the calling.
Phone number exchange in pairs: each one dictates a number (real or made up) digit by digit in Korean and the partner repeats it back to confirm.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Learn → Numbers (both systems), then Practice → Numbers in all 3 rounds (Reading, Listening, Reverse) until 3 stars.
Family flashcards (12 words) + write 6 sentences about your own family with the pattern 우리 ___은/는 ___이에요/예요.
A 40-second audio introducing 3 people from your family from a photo, without reading.
semanas.cultura: In Korea people say 우리 엄마 (our mom) and even 우리나라 (our country) instead of 'my': the 우리 reflects the collective outlook of Korean culture, and older siblings are called by their role (언니, 오빠, 형, 누나), never by name.

semanas.leccion: Lesson 5 집이 어디예요? (Where is your house?) from the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1
semanas.objetivo: Say where you live, ask where a place is and locate things with position words.
gramatica: 어디예요? (where is it?) and the answer with the name of the place: 집이 어디예요? — 산티아고예요
N에 있어요/없어요 (it is in N / it is not in N): the location particle 에 with the verb of existence
Position words 위 (above, on top), 아래 (below), 앞 (in front), 뒤 (behind), 옆 (next to), 안 (inside) + 에: 책상 위에 있어요
이/가 (subject particle) introduced only with 있어요/없어요: 책이 책상 위에 있어요
practica: Desk tour: each student describes 3 things on their desk with 위/아래/옆/안 (컴퓨터 옆에 커피가 있어요) and the others draw what they hear; then the drawings are compared on camera.
Street dialogue in pairs with the textbook map: A asks 화장실이 어디예요? / 은행이 어디예요?, B answers 카페 옆에 있어요 and A finds it on the map.
Group survey: 집이 어디예요? — each student answers with their city and country, and the teacher marks them on the shared map.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Pictograms (places and objects) and Words in Reverse mode until 3 stars.
Lesson 5 worksheet: label the drawing of the room with 위/아래/앞/뒤/옆/안 and complete 8 sentences with 에 있어요.
A photo of your desk or your room + 5 written sentences locating objects (책이 책상 위에 있어요), posted in the course community.
semanas.cultura: Addresses in Korea have used the 도로명 주소 (street-name address) system since 2014, but in practice everyone finds their way by the nearest 지하철역 (subway station) and its exit number.

semanas.leccion: Lesson 6 학교에 가요 (I go to school) from the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1
semanas.objetivo: Talk about where you go every day and what you do, conjugating your first verbs in the informal-polite present tense.
gramatica: -아요/어요 (informal-polite present): stems with ㅏ/ㅗ → -아요 (가요, 봐요), all others → -어요 (먹어요, 마셔요), 하다 → 해요
N에 가요/와요 (I go to N / I come to N): the particle 에 as destination
Time expressions without a particle: 오늘 (today), 매일 (every day), 지금 (now) at the start of the sentence
Questions 어디에 가요? (where are you going?) and 뭐 해요? (what are you doing?)
practica: Conjugation wheel with gestures: the teacher says the stem (가다) and makes the gesture, the group answers in chorus 가요; then an individual relay with the 9 verbs of the week, correcting 봐요 and 와요.
My day in 5 sentences: in pairs, each student tells 5 things they do every day (매일 회사에 가요. 커피 마셔요…) and the partner reports it to the group in the third person (마리아는 매일 회사에 가요).
Show-of-hands survey: 매일 뭐 해요? — for each verb students raise their hand (손 드세요) and the group's activity ranking is built on screen.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Time Trial: beat your own record twice (speed reading with audio) and save a screenshot of the Progress tab.
Lesson 6 worksheet: conjugation table of the week's 9 verbs in -아요/어요 + 8 sentences with N에 가요/와요.
A 45-second audio describing your typical day with at least 6 verbs in the present tense.
semanas.cultura: A Korean schoolkid spends the day between 학교 (school) and 학원 (private academy) until well into the night: the 빨리빨리 (hurry, hurry) culture starts at school.

semanas.leccion: Lesson 7 방에 침대가 있어요 (There is a bed in the room) and Lesson 8 그림을 그려요 (I draw a picture) from the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1
semanas.objetivo: Describe your room with 있어요/없어요 and say what you do with things, using the subject and object particles correctly.
gramatica: 있어요/없어요 now as 'there is / there isn't' to describe a place (in week 5 it was 'is in'): 방에 침대가 있어요, 창문이 없어요; 이/가 is consolidated marking what exists
을/를 (direct object particle): 책을 읽어요, 커피를 마셔요; 을 after a final consonant, 를 after a vowel
Contrast 은/는 vs 이/가 only with the course sentences: 저는 학생이에요 (known topic) / 책이 있어요 (new subject)
Verbs with the vowel ㅣ/ㅜ that contract in the present: 마시다 → 마셔요, 그리다 → 그려요, 배우다 → 배워요
vocabulario: 듣다 (to listen; 들어요 is learned as a fixed form)
practica: Tour of my room: each student shows their room on camera or with a photo and says 4 sentences (방에 침대가 있어요. 텔레비전은 없어요…); the group asks 컴퓨터가 있어요?
Verb charades in pairs: one acts it out (그림을 그려요, 음악을 들어요), the other guesses the full sentence with 을/를; one point is scored per correct particle.
Particle dictation: 10 sentences from the textbook with a blank; students write 이/가 or 을/를 in the chat and one student justifies each choice aloud.
tarea: Lessons 7–8 worksheet + a 15-item written quiz (particles and conjugation) to hand in before class 8.
Hangul Reader → Practice → Words and Time Trial in Listening mode: keep the 3 stars from the previous weeks.

Prepare the script for your final mini-presentation (8–10 sentences: who you are, your family, where you live, your day and your room; the sentences about your likes are added in class 8) and send it for correction before class 8.
semanas.cultura: Many Koreans sleep on a 요 (thin floor mattress) on a floor with 온돌 (underfloor heating); that's why a traditional room doesn't always have a 침대 (bed), and the furniture is low.

semanas.leccion: Lesson 9 사과를 좋아해요 (I like apples) + Lesson 10 종합연습 (comprehensive review) from the textbook 한글학교 한국어 1
semanas.objetivo: Say what you like and don't like, bring the whole course together in an oral mini-presentation and wrap up with the assessment and the certificate.
gramatica: N을/를 좋아해요 / 안 좋아해요 (I like / I don't like N): 좋아하다 takes an object with 을/를, not a subject; 안 좋아해요 is learned as a fixed phrase (the negation 안 is systematized in Basic 2)
뭘 좋아해요? (what do you like?), a contraction of 뭐를, and the answer with 정말 (really) or 조금 (a little)
Comprehensive review from Lesson 10: 이에요/예요 · 은/는 · 이/가 · 을/를 · 에 · -아요/어요 in a single text about yourself
practica: Likes survey in pairs: 김치를 좋아해요? — 네, 정말 좋아해요 / 아니요, 안 좋아해요; each pair reports one thing they have in common and one difference to the group.

Final mini-presentation 'Me in Korean': 1 to 2 minutes per student, camera on and without reading (introduction, family, where you live, your day, your room and your likes); the group asks each presenter one question.
Course wrap-up: each student says in Korean one sentence they couldn't say 8 weeks ago; the teacher presents the bridge to Basic 2 (A1.2): past, future and numbers in use.
tarea: Before class: take the online written exam (30 minutes, available 48 hours before class 8).
After class: Hangul Reader → Practice → Time Trial, a final round to log your best score and save a screenshot of the Progress tab as the course wrap-up.
Record an audio of your corrected final mini-presentation (1 minute) and keep it: it's your starting point to compare against when you finish Basic 2.
semanas.cultura: Gifting fruit in Korea is a serious gesture: boxes of 사과 (apples) or 배 (pears) are the classic gift for 추석 (harvest festival) and 설날 (Lunar New Year), and they are sold individually wrapped.

evaluacion.quizzes: A 5-minute weekly quiz at the start of each class (classes 2 through 7): 5 items on reading, vocabulary or grammar from the previous session, answered in the chat or on screen. It is corrected on the spot, counts toward participation and helps identify who needs reinforcement in the pair breakout rooms.
evaluacion.tareas: Each week, three short deliverables before the next class: (1) the Hangul Reader missions, with the stars visible in the Progress tab; (2) the textbook lesson worksheet; (3) a 20-to-45-second audio in the course community. The teacher returns brief pronunciation feedback by audio or text. Homework is considered complete when submitted in at least 6 of the 7 weeks that have homework.
evaluacion.examen_final: A 30-minute online written exam (timed form), available during the 48 hours before class 8. Four sections out of 50 points: (1) audio dictation of 10 syllables and words, including 4 with batchim (reading and listening, 10 pts); (2) two-way Korean–Spanish vocabulary from lessons 1–9 (15 pts); (3) particles 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에 and -아요/어요 conjugation (15 pts); (4) production: 6 sentences about yourself (family, home, day, likes) using the course structures (10 pts).
evaluacion.oral: Final mini-presentation 'Me in Korean' in class 8: 1 to 2 minutes with camera on and without reading (introduction, family, where you live, your day, your room and your likes) plus one question from the group. Assessed on intelligibility, use of the course structures and pronunciation of vowels and batchim; speaking slowly is not penalized. The script is submitted in week 7 and returned corrected before class.
evaluacion.certificado: Academia Seúl certificate 'Basic 1 (A1.1) · CEFR A1 (partial) · TOPIK I level 1 preparation' for anyone who scores at least 60% overall (40% participation and quizzes · 30% homework · 30% written and oral exam) and attends a minimum of 6 of the 8 live classes (≥ 75%; watching the recording does not count as attendance). Those who don't reach the minimum receive a certificate of participation and may retake the oral the following week. Delivered the week of November 30 along with the Basic 2 (A1.2) presale.

materiales: Textbook 한글학교 한국어 1 (Hangul School Korean, volume 1): covers 가나다라 I–II and lessons 1 through 9, plus the comprehensive review in lesson 10

Hangul Reader (academiaseul.com/lector-hangul): free app with native audio; tabs Alphabet, Learn, Practice (Vowels, Consonants, Aspirated and tense, Syllables, Batchim, Words, Numbers, Pictograms, Time Trial, in Reading, Listening and Reverse modes) and Progress
A deck for each session using the house trilingual template (ES/KO/EN) + an activity worksheet per lesson with the week's quiz
Zoom recording of each class, available 24 hours later
Digital flashcards for family, places, verbs and likes (weeks 4 through 8)
Academia Seúl's Korean pronunciation guide for Spanish speakers (PDF)
Course student community for submitting audios, worksheets and photos, and receiving the teacher's feedback
Notebook and pencil for tracing Hangul by hand during the first two weeks; camera and microphone in every class
notas_profesor: Pacing for weeks 1–2: the Hangul Reader does the drilling, not the class. Present each group of letters, have each student read 2 or 3 syllables aloud and send the rest to the app; if by week 3 someone still can't read batchim, offer them 10 minutes on the side before or after class, but don't slow the group down.

The five pronunciation errors of Spanish speakers that do need correcting from day 1, with mouth gestures: ㅡ pronounced as 'u', ㅓ pronounced as 'o', ㅂ/ㅍ/ㅃ and ㄱ/ㅋ/ㄲ heard as a single sound, and final ㅇ replaced with 'n'. Intonation and speed are let go at A1.1.

이에요/예요 and the particles: students want to translate 'is' and 'I' word for word. A pocket rule that works: with batchim → 이에요 / 은 / 이 / 을; without batchim → 예요 / 는 / 가 / 를. The topic-vs-subject difference (은/는 vs 이/가) is only touched on in week 7 and only with the textbook examples; don't open that topic earlier even if they ask.

In Spanish the direct object carries no marker, so 을/를 gets dropped systematically (책 읽어요). In writing, always correct it from week 7 on; in speaking, accept the omission if the sentence is understood and note it for the wrap-up, so as not to cut off someone who has just worked up the courage to speak.

Mixed group: some students will arrive from the July Level 1 or from K-dramas already reading a bit and others from absolute zero. In Zoom breakout rooms, pair a fast reader with a slow one for dictations; give the fast ones the Reverse and Time Trial modes in the Reader as a challenge, not more grammar.

Explain grammar in Spanish (it's your advantage as a bilingual), but keep classroom commands, greetings and pronunciation corrections always in Korean: 따라 하세요, 다시 한번, 잘했어요. Use the group's real names in every example and avoid getting ahead with telling time and the full native numbers: they belong to Basic 2, and loading week 4 with that breaks the class.

Ask for homework audios from week 1 (20 to 45 seconds) and reply to each one with a 15-second audio of your own: it's the habit that keeps the group engaged the most. For class 8, collect the mini-presentation scripts in week 7, return them corrected, and in the live class time 2 minutes per student so all 15 fit; close with the explicit bridge to Basic 2 (past, future, numbers in use).

descripcion: The continuation of Basic 1 (A1.1) and the July Level 1: from present to past and future. In 8 weeks you go from isolated sentences to telling what you did, describing your routine and planning what you'll do, and you add the particles that make your Korean sound natural (보다, 처럼, 마다, 밖에…). Reading and numbers are drilled in the Hangul Reader; the live hour is for speaking and being corrected. Ends with the in-house A2 exam and an assessed conversation, your direct pass into Conversational 1 (A2.1).
perfil_alumno: Spanish-speaking adults from Latin America and Spain who completed Basic 1 (A1.1) or the July 2026 Level 1 course: they read Hangul fluently (batchim included), introduce themselves, use 이에요/예요 (to be), 있어요/없어요 (there is / to have) and the present tense -아요/어요 with about 10 verbs, and want to go from isolated sentences to telling their life story in three tenses. Also self-taught learners who passed the free placement test. They study at night after work: the course asks for one live hour and about 2 hours of homework spread across the week.
requisito_entrada: Academia Seúl's Basic 1 (A1.1) or the July 2026 Level 1 course, passed; or the free placement test (academiaseul.com/test-nivel). In practice: read any syllable in Hangul, introduce yourself (저는 ~예요), handle 이에요/예요 and 있어요/없어요, count with Sino-Korean numbers and form the present tense -아요/어요 with regular verbs. The alphabet is not taught in this course.
objetivos: Talk about your routine, your past and your plans using all three tenses: -아요/어요 (present), -았어요/었어요 (past) and -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (future)
Use Sino-Korean and native Korean numbers in real life: age, birthday, time (몇 시) and phone number
Say what you don't do, what you can't do and what you know how to do with 안, 못 and -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요/없어요
Compare and be precise like a native speaker with the particles 보다, 처럼, 마다, 밖에, 만, 도 and 한테
Link sentences with -고 (and) and -지만 (but) and hold a conversation in Korean for 5 minutes straight without falling back on Spanish
Pass the in-house A2 exam and the oral assessment, and be ready for Conversational 1 (A2.1)

estructura_clase.detalle: 5 quick questions (conjugation, particle or number) on last week's class; the homework sheet is corrected on screen. Activates memory before adding anything new.

The 2–4 grammar points from the textbook unit, with drawings, gestures and examples from the students' real lives; explicit contrast with Spanish. Students produce a sentence of their own from the very first example.
Fast oral chain: Jay throws out a verb or a sentence and each student transforms it (present ↔ past ↔ future, affirmative ↔ negative). Pronunciation corrected on the fly.
Role play, interview or mini-diary in Zoom breakout rooms of two; Jay rotates through the rooms and corrects one on one. This is the block that never gets cut.
Three students sum up the class in one sentence in Korean; the week's homework is explained (session worksheet + Hangul Reader or a short audio) and the next quiz is previewed.

semanas.leccion: Wednesday, October 7 · Textbook Fundamentals 01–02: 이다 (to be) and 있다 (there is / to have / to be located) · active review of Basic 1 · individual oral diagnostic
semanas.objetivo: You introduce yourself again in detail (name, country and city, occupation, family, hobby) and answer simple questions about yourself without reading; Jay takes your oral diagnostic as the baseline for the course.
gramatica: N이에요/예요 (to be, polite present) and N이/가 아니에요 (not to be): 저는 학생이 아니에요
있어요/없어요 (there is · to have · to be located) with N에 (in/at): 집에 강아지가 있어요
은/는 (topic) vs. 이/가 (subject): contrastive review with the question words 뭐 (what), 누구 (who), 어디 (where)
Polite style -아요/어요 from Basic 1 reactivated with 살다 (to live), 일하다 (to work), 공부하다 (to study)
practica: Re-introduction round: each student introduces themselves in 4–5 sentences (name, country or city, occupation, hobby) and ends with a question to another classmate (취미가 뭐예요?)
Pair interview with a cue card: 어디에 살아요? 형제가 있어요? 요즘 뭐 해요? — then each student introduces their partner to the group in the third person

2-minute individual oral diagnostic with Jay in a separate breakout room, while the rest play '있어요/없어요' with the objects on their desks (in class 1 there is no quiz or drill: those 10 minutes are added to the pair block so all 15 students get their turn)
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Syllables and Batchim in Listening mode until 3 stars: get your reading speed back before class 2
Worksheet 1: complete 10 sentences with 이에요/예요, 있어요/없어요 and the correct particle (은/는 · 이/가), plus 3 sentences about your family
30-second audio via the course WhatsApp group: your re-introduction in 5 sentences, without reading
semanas.cultura: When meeting someone in Korea, handshakes are rare: you give a small bow (인사) and say 반갑습니다; asking someone's age when you first meet isn't rude, it helps you know how to address them.

semanas.leccion: Wednesday, October 14 · Textbook Fundamentals 03–05: Sino-Korean and native Korean numerals · dates and days of the week · telling time (몇 시)
semanas.objetivo: You say your age, your birthday, your phone number and the time you do things, and you understand that information when it's said to you at normal speed.
gramatica: Sino-Korean numerals (일, 이, 삼…), reactivated from Basic 1, now for dates, phone numbers, minutes and prices
Native Korean numerals (하나, 둘, 셋…) with 살 (years of age) and 시 (o'clock); short forms 한 · 두 · 세 · 네 before the counter
몇 (how many / what number): 몇 시예요? (what time is it?) · 몇 살이에요? (how old are you?) · 며칠이에요? (what's the date?)
N에 (at / on, for time): 세 시에 (at three), 월요일에 (on Monday), 생일에 (on one's birthday)
vocabulario: 요일 (day of the week: 월요일 … 일요일)
practica: Chain number dictation: Jay dictates phone numbers and dates, each student writes them down and then dictates their own number (real or made up) to a partner, who repeats it back to confirm
Human clock in pairs: one says a time (여덟 시 반) and the other writes it in digits; then they ask each other 몇 시에 일어나요? (what time do you get up?) and 몇 시에 자요? (what time do you go to bed?)
Birthday mini-survey: each student asks 생일이 언제예요? to three classmates and the group builds the course birthday calendar on screen
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Numbers: all three rounds (Sino-Korean, native and mixed) in Reading and Listening modes until 3 stars
Worksheet 2: write in Hangul your age, your birthday, your phone number and three times of your day (getting up, lunch, bedtime)
Short audio: the times of your routine on a normal day, 5 sentences with N에 (일곱 시에 일어나요…)
semanas.cultura: A Korean can state their age in two ways: the traditional 'Korean age' (you're born at one and add a year every New Year) and the international age, the only official one since June 2023; that's why you'll sometimes hear two numbers for the same person.

semanas.leccion: Wednesday, October 21 · Textbook Tenses unit 01–02: the full polite present -아요/어요 and the formal present -ㅂ니다/습니다 · everyday irregular verbs · the particle 에서 vs. 에
semanas.objetivo: You describe your real routine with 10 verbs in the present tense, including the most frequent irregulars, and you recognize the formal style -ㅂ니다/습니다 when you hear it in stores, on the news and in presentations.
gramatica: -아요/어요 (polite present) reactivated from Basic 1: the vowel rule (ㅏ/ㅗ → -아요, everything else → -어요, 하다 → 해요) and contractions (가요, 봐요, 마셔요)
Everyday irregulars: ㅂ (덥다 → 더워요), ㄷ (듣다 → 들어요), 으 (바쁘다 → 바빠요), 르 (모르다 → 몰라요), ㄹ (살다 → 삽니다)
-ㅂ니다/습니다 (formal present), only to recognize it and use it in a brief self-introduction
N에서 (in/at, the place where something is done) vs. N에 (in / to, location or destination): 회사에서 일해요 · 회사에 가요
practica: Fast conjugation wheel: a card with the dictionary form on screen, the student says the -아요/어요 form within 3 seconds; irregulars count double
My routine in pairs: each student narrates their day with 8–10 verbs and times (일곱 시에 일어나요, 여덟 시에 출근해요…); the partner takes notes and tells the other's routine to the group
Selective listening: Jay reads 6 sentences mixing -아요/어요 and -ㅂ니다/습니다; students mark which is which and whom they would say it to (a friend, a client)
tarea: Conjugation worksheet 3: table of 20 verbs (12 regular and 8 irregular) in -아요/어요 and -ㅂ니다/습니다
Hangul Reader → Practice → Words and Time Trial in Listening mode (10 minutes): keep your 3 stars from Basic 1 and your reading speed
10-question online quiz on the present tense and irregulars (reviewed in the opening quiz of class 4)
semanas.cultura: In a Korean office the greeting changes with the time of day: 안녕하세요 when you arrive and, if you leave before your colleagues, 먼저 가겠습니다 (I'm leaving first); slipping out in silence gets noticed.

semanas.leccion: Wednesday, October 28 · Textbook Tenses unit 03: past tense -았어요/었어요 · Particles unit 08: 부터~까지 (from… to) · past time expressions · 하고 / (이)랑 (with whom)
semanas.objetivo: You tell what you did over the weekend or on your last vacation in 6–8 linked sentences, saying when, where and with whom.
gramatica: -았어요/었어요 (past): same vowel rule as the present (갔어요, 먹었어요, 했어요) and N이었어요/였어요 for nouns (학생이었어요)
N부터 N까지 (from… to, for time) and N에서 N까지 (from… to, for places): 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지 일했어요
Time expressions with and without 에: 어제 (yesterday), 지난주에 (last week), 오늘 아침에 (this morning), 작년에 (last year)
N하고 / N(이)랑 (with, and) to say who with: 친구하고 영화를 봤어요
practica: Oral mini-diary: each student tells about their last weekend in 5 past-tense sentences; the group asks them two questions (누구하고 갔어요? 어디에서 먹었어요?)
Transformation chain: Jay says a sentence in the present, the next student switches it to the past and adds a time expression (어제…, 지난주에…), and so on around the circle
Fictional schedule in pairs: with a made-up work schedule, they ask and answer 몇 시부터 몇 시까지 일했어요? and 어디에서 어디까지 갔어요?
tarea: Written mini-diary: 3 past-tense sentences about your day today, sent via the course WhatsApp group (photo of your notebook or text)
Hangul Reader → Practice → Numbers in Reverse mode (10 minutes): so the hours in 부터~까지 (아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지) come out without thinking
Worksheet 4: switch 15 sentences from present to past and complete a short text with 부터~까지
semanas.cultura: A typical weekend in Seoul is told with 카페에 갔어요 and 집에서 쉬었어요: Korea has one of the highest densities of coffee shops in the world, and the café is the default place to meet up, study and rest.

semanas.leccion: Wednesday, November 4 · Textbook Tenses unit 04: future and intention -(으)ㄹ 거예요 · Listing and contrast unit 02: -거나 (or) · Particles 13: (으)로 (means of transportation)
semanas.objetivo: You plan your dream vacation or your next week: you say what you're going to do, when, how and with whom, and you offer alternatives (A or B).
gramatica: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (future / intention): -ㄹ 거예요 after a vowel (갈 거예요), -을 거예요 after a consonant (먹을 거예요); watch out for a final ㄹ (살 거예요)
-거나 (or, between verbs): 영화를 보거나 쉴 거예요 (I'll watch a movie or rest) vs. N(이)나 between nouns (커피나 차)
Future time expressions: 내일 (tomorrow), 다음 주에 (next week), 이번 주말에 (this weekend), 내년에 (next year)
N(으)로 (by, means of transportation): 비행기로 갈 거예요 (I'll go by plane), 기차로 (by train)
practica: Dream vacation in pairs: each student puts together a 3-day plan (어디에 갈 거예요? 언제? 뭐 할 거예요? 뭐로 갈 거예요?) and presents it to the group in 6 sentences
'Let's meet up' role play: suggest a day and an activity for next week using -거나 (토요일에 영화를 보거나 산에 갈 거예요?), and accept or suggest something else
Three tenses, one sentence: Jay throws out a verb and a time word (어제 / 오늘 / 내일); the student answers in the past, present or future as appropriate
tarea: Worksheet 5: complete a travel itinerary with -(으)ㄹ 거예요, -거나 and (으)로 (12 blanks) and write your own weekend plan in 4 sentences
Hangul Reader → Practice → Time Trial: one timed round, then save your Progress screen with your score
10-question online quiz: future tense and time expressions (reviewed at the start of class 6)
semanas.cultura: Summer vacations in Korea are short: many workers take only 3–5 consecutive days in late July or early August, which is why the typical trip is intense: Jeju, Busan or Japan over a long weekend.

semanas.leccion: Wednesday, November 11 · Textbook Negation unit 01–03: 안 / -지 않아요 · 못 / -지 못해요 · negatives that are words of their own · Ability unit 01: -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요/없어요
semanas.objetivo: You say what you don't do (by choice), what you can't do (due to circumstances) and what you know how to do, and you answer yes/no questions naturally and with a reason.
gramatica: 안 + verb/adjective (in Basic 1 only with 안 좋아해요) and -지 않아요 (not, negation by choice or state): 안 먹어요 / 먹지 않아요; with N하다 verbs, 안 goes in the middle (운동 안 해요)
못 + verb and -지 못해요 (can't, due to circumstances or lack of ability): 못 가요 / 가지 못해요
-(으)ㄹ 수 있어요/없어요 (can / can't, ability or possibility): 수영할 수 있어요, 매운 음식을 먹을 수 없어요
Negatives that are words of their own: 있다 → 없다, 알다 → 모르다, 좋아하다 → 싫어하다
practica: 'Can you…?' survey: each student asks three classmates 수영할 수 있어요? 운전할 수 있어요? 기타를 칠 수 있어요? and reports back to the group in the third person (마리아 씨는 운전할 수 있어요)
'The invitation I can't accept' role play: A invites for tomorrow (내일 같이 영화 볼 거예요?), B declines with 못 and gives a reason in the past or future; then they switch roles
Three cards, three negations: given a situation (I'm on a diet, I don't have a car, I don't like spicy food) the student chooses 안, 못 or -(으)ㄹ 수 없어요 and explains why they chose that form
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Time Trial: beat the score you saved in week 5 (Progress screen)
Negation worksheet 6: choose 안 / 못 / -(으)ㄹ 수 없어요 in 15 situations and write 5 things you can do and 5 you can't
40-second audio: '할 수 있어요, 못 해요' (what I can and can't do), 6 sentences mixing ability and negation
semanas.cultura: Turning down an invitation in Korea is rarely a flat 'no': you use 못 with a reason (일이 있어서 못 가요) and often 다음에 (next time), even if there is no next time; it's courtesy, not a promise.

semanas.leccion: Wednesday, November 18 · Textbook Particles unit (selection): 05 의 · 09 에게/한테 · 10 도 · 11 만 · 12 밖에 · 14 쯤 · 15 처럼 · 16 보다 · 17 마다
semanas.objetivo: You compare, specify and add nuance to what you say ('only', 'also', 'more than', 'like', 'every', 'to whom') and sound Korean, not translated; you also recognize the particles when you hear them, as the exam requires.
gramatica: Comparing: N보다 (more than) with 더 (more) and N처럼 (like): 형은 저보다 키가 커요 · 한국 사람처럼 말해요
Limiting and adding: N만 (only), N밖에 + negation (nothing but) and N도 (also): 커피만 마셔요 · 천 원밖에 없어요 · 저도 가요
Frequency and approximation: N마다 (every) and N쯤 (around, approximately): 주말마다 운동해요 · 세 시쯤 만나요
Possession and recipient: N의 ('s / of; contracts to 제 / 내 and is often dropped) and N한테 / N에게 (to someone): 친구한테 선물을 줬어요
practica: Comparison in pairs: with three pairs of photos (two cities, two dishes, two idols) each student says 3 sentences with 보다 / 더 and 처럼, and the partner reacts (저도요 / 저는 아니에요)
'All I have is…': each student describes what's on their desk with 만 and 밖에 (펜밖에 없어요, 커피만 있어요); Jay reads the sentences shuffled and the group guesses whose desk each one is
Particle dictation (exam format): Jay reads 8 sentences and students write only the particle they hear; corrected on screen right away
tarea: Particle worksheet 7 in exam format: 20 blanks (은/는 · 이/가 · 을/를 · 에 · 에서 · 도 · 만 · 밖에 · 보다 · 마다 · 한테); due before class 8
Review the vocabulary of weeks 1–7 with the worksheets: mark the 20 words that don't come out on their own and drill them out loud until they do (prep for the vocabulary section of the exam)
Write 5 sentences comparing your country with Korea (보다 / 처럼 / 도) and record them as audio
semanas.cultura: Two particles from this class are heard all day long in Korea: 밖에 in shops (하나밖에 안 남았어요, 'there's only one left', the favorite sales line) and 만 hidden inside 잠깐만요 ('just a moment', literally 'only a moment'), what you say to get through a crowd on the subway or to ask someone to wait a second.

semanas.leccion: Wednesday, November 25 · Textbook Listing and contrast unit 01 and 03: -고 (and) · -지만 (but) · integration of the 7 classes · in-house A2 exam + oral assessment · certificate
semanas.objetivo: You hold a 5-minute conversation in Korean about your life, your past and your plans, linking sentences with -고 and -지만, and you take the in-house A2 exam.
gramatica: -고 (and, listing or sequence): 밥을 먹고 커피를 마셨어요; the tense is marked only on the last verb
-지만 (but, contrast): 한국어는 어렵지만 재미있어요
Integration: present, past and future + negation + particles in a single 8–10 sentence narrative
practica: Connector warm-up (10 min): quickly chain pairs of sentences from the course with -고 and -지만; each student produces two
Written A2 exam online (30 min, timed, with Jay present): two-way vocabulary, particles, tenses and dates/times, translation and personal production

Oral assessment (20 min): 5-minute conversations in pairs in Zoom breakout rooms with a card of 6 topics (routine, last weekend, vacation plan, what you can do, your family, Korea and your country); Jay rotates through the rooms and scores with the rubric
tarea: Before class: review worksheets 1–7 and take the short practice exam (10 questions) shared the Monday before
After class: record your '1-minute introduction in three tenses' (who I am, what I did in this course, what I'll do in Conversational 1) and upload it to the group
After class: Hangul Reader → Practice → Time Trial, one final round to log your best score and save your Progress screen as a wrap-up (recommended, not required)
semanas.cultura: When an exam or a course ends in Korea, people say 수고했어요 (good job; literally 'you put in the effort'): effort is acknowledged before results, and the certificate is handed over and received with both hands.

evaluacion.quizzes: 5-minute quiz at the start of classes 2 through 7 (6 quizzes; in class 8 the exam replaces it): 5 questions on the previous class (conjugate a verb, choose a particle, write a number or time in Hangul). Corrected on the spot and counted within the 40% participation grade along with attendance and pair-work participation. In addition, two 10-question online quizzes (weeks 3 and 5) reviewed in the following class.
evaluacion.tareas: Every week: the session worksheet (10–20 sentences) plus a short Hangul Reader task (Practice → Syllables, Batchim, Numbers, Words or Time Trial) or a short 30–40 second audio via the course WhatsApp group. Estimated workload: 2 hours per week. Reviewed in the opening quiz and with brief feedback from Jay in the group. Weight: 30%. At least 6 of 7 submissions are required; the week 7 particle worksheet is mandatory because it follows the exam format.
evaluacion.examen_final: In-house A2 exam, written online, 30 timed minutes within class 8, 40 points in 4 sections: (1) two-way vocabulary Spanish → Korean and Korean → Spanish (10 points); (2) particles: choose the correct one in 10 blanks (은/는 · 이/가 · 을/를 · 에 · 에서 · 도 · 만 · 밖에 · 보다 · 마다 · 한테) (10 points); (3) tenses and data: switch sentences to the past and the future, write dates and times in Hangul (10 points); (4) translation of 6 sentences with -아요/어요 and -았어요/었어요 and personal production of 5 sentences about yourself (10 points). Returned graded within the week. The final exam (written + oral) is worth 30%.
evaluacion.oral: Two moments. 2-minute individual oral diagnostic in class 1 (baseline, not graded). Final oral assessment in class 8: 5-minute conversation in pairs on 6 course topics, in Zoom breakout rooms, with Jay rotating and scoring with a 4-criterion rubric (fluency without falling back on Spanish · correct use of present, past and future · particles · pronunciation). Anyone who can't be heard in class sends a 3-minute audio answering the same questions within 48 hours.
evaluacion.certificado: Academia Seúl certificate 'Basic 2 (A1.2) · full CEFR A1 (partial A2) · TOPIK I levels 1–2 preparation', issued the week of November 30, 2026. Requirements: overall grade ≥ 60% (40% participation and quizzes · 30% homework · 30% written + oral A2 exam) and attendance ≥ 75% (6 of 8 live classes; watching the recording does not count as attendance). With the certificate you go straight into Conversational 1 (A2.1) without a placement test; anyone below 60% receives a reinforcement plan and can retake the oral before the January cohort.

materiales: Korean Grammar in Use · Beginning (Spanish edition: Uso de la gramática coreana · Nivel inicial): units Fundamentals 01–05, Tenses 01–04, Negation 01–03, Particles (05, 08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17), Listing and contrast 01–03 and Ability 01
Trilingual ES/KO/EN slide deck for each session (PDF in the group after class)
Activity worksheets 1–7 (one per session) + particle worksheet in exam format
Hangul Reader (academiaseul.com/lector-hangul, free, with native audio): Practice → Syllables, Batchim, Numbers, Words and Time Trial as short weekly homework, with stars in the Progress tab
Recording of each class available 24 hours later
Course the course WhatsApp group group for audio homework, mini-diary and questions between classes
In-house A2 exam online + oral assessment rubric
Zoom with breakout rooms for pair work
notas_profesor: The group arrives mixed (Guiran's Basic 1, the July Level 1 and someone via placement test): use the class 1 oral diagnostic to set up 'strong + medium' pairs, never 'strong + strong', and don't re-explain Hangul live; send slow readers to the Reader with a concrete goal.

The Spanish speaker's core error: mixing up 'ser' and 'estar' (저는 집이에요* instead of 집에 있어요) and confusing 에 with 에서 (회사에 일해요*). Always correct these, from class 1 on, because the past and future are built on top of them.

With -았어요/었어요 and -(으)ㄹ 거예요 the most common error is the vowel rule (먹았어요*, 가을 거예요*): fix it with 3-second oral drills and gestures (hand up for ㅏ/ㅗ), not with long tables. The written form gets polished on the worksheet.

Particles: don't chase perfection on 은/는 vs. 이/가 in the first weeks; correct 을/를 and 에/에서, which pay off most on the exam, and leave the fine 은/는 contrast for week 7, when it comes back alongside 도 and 만.

Pronunciation worth correcting: the support vowel they add after batchim (밥 → 바브*), the ㅓ/ㅗ distinction and the tense consonants ㄲ/ㄸ/ㅃ. Let slide for now: intonation and the intervocalic ㄹ; those get refined in Conversational 1 with Abby.

Pacing: 25 minutes of slides is the cap and pair practice never gets cut. Class 7 (particles) is the densest: if you're running short on time, cut examples, not activities; 쯤 and 의 can be left as home reading if the group is going slow.

Differentiation: give fast learners -고 있어요 (to be doing) and the formal -ㅂ니다/습니다 as an extra on the worksheet; for slower learners, cut the week 3 verb list down to 6 and ask only for the audio, not the worksheet. In class 8 open the exam at minute 10, keep the timer running while you rotate through the rooms, and announce that same day who moves on to Conversational 1 (A2.1) and who would benefit from reinforcement.

descripcion: Pure speaking: a course where only Korean is spoken, with a native Korean teacher. Five modules on the Korea you love (K-pop and fan culture, trips to 제주도 (Jeju) and Seoul, food culture, 한복 (traditional dress) and aesthetics, PC방 (internet café) and e-sports) plus two small-group conversation labs. Each module loads 2–4 structures from Korean Grammar in Use that are cited only when needed: culture is the vehicle and grammar is the means. A2.1 certificate included and direct entry to Conversational 2 (A2.2, January 2027).
perfil_alumno: Spanish-speaking adult (Latin America or Spain) who finished Basic 2 (A1.2) or comes in through the placement test: reads Hangul fluently, handles basic present, past and future and some 300–400 words, but still "thinks in Spanish" before speaking. Is a fan of something Korean (K-pop, dramas, food, travel or video games) and wants to stop studying grammar and start talking about what they love, even if doing so in front of a native teacher makes them nervous. Group of at most 15 people; for most, class falls after the workday.
requisito_entrada: Basic 2 (A1.2) passed or the free placement test (academiaseul.com/test-nivel or via WhatsApp, 10 minutes). Specifically: read Hangul without sounding out letters, conjugate -아요/어요 (present), -았/었어요 (past) and -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (future), use the particles 이/가, 을/를, 에 and 에서, and hold 2–3 minutes of simple conversation about yourself and your routine. No need to know about K-pop or video games: the topics are the excuse to talk, not the requirement.
objetivos: Introduce yourself in detail and hold a 5-minute conversation with a native teacher without switching to Spanish
Talk about your group, your 최애 (absolute favorite) and your experiences as a fan using -아/어 봤어요 (experience), superlatives and -아서/어서 (because)
Plan a trip around Korea with a partner (propose, decide, indicate transportation) and narrate a trip in the past tense
Order at a restaurant using counters, recommend a dish and describe flavors like a local
Describe clothing and aesthetics, compare and give nuanced opinions using N보다 (more than), -아/어 보여요 (looks) and -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같아요 (it seems to me)
Talk about your free time and the gaming world with expressions of time and condition: -(으)ㄹ 때 (when) and -(으)면 (if)
Pass the A2.1 oral assessment and be ready for Conversational 2 (A2.2, January 2027)

estructura_clase.detalle: Five quick questions on the previous module (vocabulary and one structure), answered out loud or in the Zoom chat; questions about the audio homework are cleared up.
