semanas.leccion: Tuesday, October 6 · Orientation session (no themed module) · individual oral diagnostic
semanas.objetivo: Break the ice with the group and with Abby, introduce yourself in more detail than in Basic 2 (what you do, how long you've been studying Korean and why) and set your 3 personal conversation goals for the 8 weeks.
gramatica: -고 싶어요 (want to do) · to state your goals for the course · 한국어로 말하고 싶어요
-(으)ㄴ 지 ... 됐어요 (it has been ... since) · 한국어를 배운 지 6개월 됐어요
Reactivation: -아요/어요 (present), -았/었어요 (past) and -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (future) within the self-introduction
Reactivation: -고 (and), -지만 (but) and 그래서 (so, that's why) from Basic 2 to link your introduction and explain why you study Korean
practica: Chain introductions round: each student introduces themselves (name, country, occupation, how long they've been studying and why) and asks the next one a question

Pair interview in Zoom breakout rooms (3 rounds of 6 minutes, switching partners) with 5 guiding questions about what you love about Korea; back in the main room, each one introduces their last partner to the group

Oral diagnostic: while the interview runs, Abby drops into each room for 2–3 minutes, listens to both students and notes 3 data points per student (fluency, pronunciation, personal goal); anyone she doesn't get to is assessed from the homework audio. Wrap-up: each student tells the group one goal with -고 싶어요
tarea: 60–90 second audio: extended self-introduction (name, country, work or studies, how long you've been studying Korean and why). Save it: in week 8 you record it again to compare
Write 3 conversation goals with -고 싶어요 and send them via the course WhatsApp group (example: 콘서트에서 한국어로 말하고 싶어요)
Optional warm-up: Hangul Reader, Time Trial tab, one round to get your reading speed back before module 1
semanas.cultura: In Korea, asking someone's age when you first meet is normal: it isn't rude, it helps decide whether to speak in 존댓말 (formal speech) or 반말 (informal speech).

semanas.leccion: Tuesday, October 13 · M01 · K-pop and fan culture (in-house trilingual deck)
semanas.objetivo: Talk about your group, your 최애 (absolute favorite) and concerts: share experiences as a fan, express preferences with superlatives and explain why you like them with -아서/어서.
gramatica: -아/어 봤어요 (have done, experience) · 콘서트에 가 봤어요?
제일 / 가장 + adjective (superlative; 제일 already seen in Basic 2) · 제일 좋아하는 노래
N 중에서 (among, out of) · 멤버 중에서 누가 제일 좋아요?
-아서/어서 (because, cause) · 노래가 좋아서 이 그룹을 좋아해요
practica: Mini-presentation 'My 최애 (favorite) in 5 sentences' with a photo shared on screen: who they are, since when you've followed them and why
Pair role play: convince a friend to go to a concert (date, price, what to bring) and answer their questions
Lightning survey: go around the room with -아/어 봤어요 (have you been to a concert?, have you sung in Korean?) and report 2 results to the group
tarea: 90-second audio recommending a Korean song: who it's by, what it's like and why you recommend it
Write 5 sentences about a real or imagined concert using -아/어 봤어요 and 제일
Listen to a song by your group with the lyrics in Hangul and note down 5 words you recognize without a translator
semanas.cultura: Every group has a fandom with its own name and a 응원법 (fan chant) that fans memorize to shout in unison at the exact moment during the concert.

semanas.leccion: Tuesday, October 20 · M02 · Travel: Jeju and Seoul (in-house trilingual deck)
semanas.objetivo: Plan a trip with a partner (propose, decide, explain how to get around) and narrate a past trip by chaining sentences in the past tense.
gramatica: -(으)ㄹ까요? (shall we...?, how about...?) · 제주도에 갈까요?
-(으)러 가요 (go to + purpose) · 바다를 보러 가요
N(으)로 (means of transportation, already seen in Basic 2) extended to direction · 비행기로, 지하철로, 왼쪽으로, 홍대로
-아서/어서 extended: sequence (and then), besides the cause from week 2 · 공항에 가서 비행기를 타요
practica: Travel agency in pairs: plan 3 days in 제주도 (Jeju Island) on a given budget, deciding each step with -(으)ㄹ까요? and presenting the plan in 1 minute
Role play 'on the Seoul subway' with the real map on screen: ask how to get from 명동 (shopping district) to 홍대 (university area) using N(으)로
Chain story: each student adds a past-tense sentence to the group's travel story with -았/었어요 and -아서/어서
tarea: Written 2-day itinerary in Korea (6–8 sentences) with transportation, places and one meal
90-second audio: 'my dream trip to Korea' or a real trip you took, with at least 3 verbs in the past or future
Look at the Seoul subway map (link provided) and write in Hangul 5 stations you'd like to visit
semanas.cultura: On 제주도 (Jeju Island) the 돌하르방 (stone grandfathers) guard the entrances to houses and villages; tradition says touching their nose brings good luck, which is why many have worn-down noses.

semanas.leccion: Tuesday, October 27 · M03 · Food culture (in-house trilingual deck)
semanas.objetivo: Order at a Korean restaurant with counters and politeness, recommend a dish and describe flavors; understand an order spoken at natural speed.
gramatica: -아/어 주세요 (please give me / please do for me) · 물 좀 주세요
Counters: 개 (items), 병 (bottles) and 잔 (glasses) with native numerals (한 개, 두 병, 세 잔); 인분 (servings) with Sino-Korean numerals · 삼겹살 이 인분 주세요
-지 마세요 (please don't + verb, polite negative request) · 너무 맵게 하지 마세요
-(으)ㄴ + N (adjective as modifier) · 매운 음식, 단 음식
practica: Role play 'at the restaurant' with a real menu on screen: customer and 사장님 (owner) order and serve for 3 people using counters and one special request
'Recommend me something': each student recommends a dish from their country describing 3 flavors; the group votes on which one they want to try
Order dictation: Abby reads 3 orders at natural speed and students note down what and how much each table ordered
tarea: 60–90 second audio recommending a Korean dish or one from your country with at least 3 flavor adjectives
Write a complete order for 3 people (dishes, quantities with counters and one request with -지 마세요)
Look up the menu of a Seoul restaurant on 네이버 (Korean search engine) or Google Maps and translate 5 dishes
semanas.cultura: At a Korean restaurant the 반찬 (side dishes) are refilled for free as many times as you like, and to call the staff you say 여기요 (over here, please) or 사장님 (owner) out loud, without being shy.

semanas.leccion: Tuesday, November 3 · Lab 1 · integrates M01–M03 (K-pop, travel, food) · no new deck
semanas.objetivo: Hold 10 straight minutes of conversation in groups of 3 on the topics from weeks 2–4, solving real tasks (deciding, ordering, negotiating), and receive one-on-one pronunciation correction.
gramatica: Active review: -아/어 봤어요 (experience) to tell and ask
Active review: -(으)ㄹ까요? / 같이 -아요/어요 (proposing and accepting a plan)
Active review: -아/어 주세요 + counters (ordering at a restaurant)
Repair strategies: 다시 한번 말해 주세요 (please say it again), 무슨 뜻이에요? (what does it mean?)
practica: Three stations in 3-person Zoom breakout rooms, 10 minutes each with rotation: 'travel agency', 'restaurant' and 'fan meetup'; each station comes with a card stating the task and a concrete outcome (plan, order, recommendation)
Final real-world group task: negotiate a weekend in Seoul on a budget and present the decision in 1 minute; the group must reach agreement in Korean only
One-on-one correction: Abby rotates through the rooms and notes 2 pronunciation errors per student; she returns them at wrap-up with a model and repetition
tarea: 2-minute audio: 'a perfect weekend in Korea' integrating a concert, a trip and food
Written self-assessment (in Spanish is fine): 3 things I said well and 2 I want to improve before Lab 2
Review the class recording and note down 3 phrases from your classmates you'd like to use
semanas.cultura: In a Korean conversation, 맞장구 (backchannel responses: 네, 맞아요, 그렇구나) are used constantly to show you're listening; staying completely silent comes across as cold or uninterested.

semanas.leccion: Tuesday, November 10 · M04 · Hanbok and aesthetics (in-house trilingual deck)
semanas.objetivo: Describe clothing, colors and patterns, compare traditional with modern and give your nuanced opinion on 한복 (traditional Korean dress) and Korean aesthetics.
gramatica: Reactivation: -(으)ㄴ + N (week 4) and N보다 더 (Basic 2) · 예쁜 한복, 한복이 청바지보다 더 화려해요
-아/어 보여요 (looks + adjective) · 편해 보여요, 비싸 보여요
-(으)ㄴ/는 것 같아요 (it seems to me that) · 전통 한복이 더 예쁜 것 같아요
-지만 (but) reactivated for nuanced opinions · 예쁘지만 불편해요
vocabulario: 저고리 (short jacket of the traditional dress)
어울리다 (to suit, to go well with)
practica: 'Stylist for a day': in pairs, choose a 한복 (traditional dress) for a photo at 경복궁 (Gyeongbokgung Palace) from 4 options on screen and justify color, pattern and comfort
Chain opinions: traditional or modern 한복; each student must use N보다, -지만 and 것 같아요 on their turn
Blind description: one student describes a photo of a 한복 and their partner picks it out of 3 options without seeing it
tarea: Write 6–8 sentences describing your favorite outfit or a 한복 (traditional dress) you'd like to wear: colors, pattern, how it looks and what it goes with
60–90 second opinion audio: modern or traditional 한복? with at least two comparisons
Find a photo of a 한복 on Instagram or Pinterest and note down in Hangul 3 colors and 2 adjectives that describe it
semanas.cultura: If you visit 경복궁 (Gyeongbokgung Palace) or the other palaces in Seoul wearing 한복 (traditional dress), admission is free: that's why the streets of 북촌 (traditional hanok village) fill up with colorfully dressed visitors.

semanas.leccion: Tuesday, November 17 · M05 · PC방 and e-sports (in-house trilingual deck)
semanas.objetivo: Talk about video games, free time and technology: say when and how much you play, what you're good or bad at, express conditions and hold a mini-debate about gamer Korea.
gramatica: -(으)ㄹ 때 (when) · 게임할 때 컵라면을 먹어요
-기 전에 / -(으)ㄴ 후에 (before / after) · 게임하기 전에, 수업이 끝난 후에
잘 / 못 + verb (ability: well / can't) reactivated from Basic 2 · 저는 게임을 잘 못해요
-(으)면 (if, conditional when) · 이기면 기분이 좋아요
practica: Role play 'at the PC방 (internet café)': ask for 2 hours and a 컵라면 (cup ramen) and ask the 사장님 (owner) the hourly price
Pair survey 'when and how much do you play' with -(으)ㄹ 때 and 마다 (every); then each one shares their partner's most curious habit
Mini-debate in two teams: 'are e-sports a sport?' with 저는 ... 것 같아요 and -지만; Abby moderates and notes the opinion expressions that come up
tarea: 90-second audio about your digital pastime (game, app, drama or music) using -(으)ㄹ 때 and -기 전에 / -(으)ㄴ 후에
Write 5 sentences with -(으)면: what you do if you win, if you lose, if you have free time
Watch 2 minutes of an LCK (Korean League of Legends league) highlights recap with subtitles and note down 5 words you recognize
semanas.cultura: The PC방 (internet café) is part of Korean social life: it costs around 1,500 원 (won) per hour, food is served right at your seat, and LCK finals are watched on giant screens with thousands of fans in the streets.

semanas.leccion: Tuesday, November 24 · Lab 2 (M01–M05) + end-of-stage oral assessment · certificate and invitation to Conversational 2
semanas.objetivo: Demonstrate in the end-of-stage oral assessment (audios sent before class + pair role play with Abby) that you can converse about the course's five topics integrating the structures learned, and close with personal feedback, the A2.1 certificate and an invitation to Conversational 2 (A2.2, January 2027).
gramatica: Integration 1: telling experiences and proposing plans (-아/어 봤어요, -(으)ㄹ까요?, -(으)러 가요)
Integration 2: ordering, describing and giving opinions (-아/어 주세요 + counters, -(으)ㄴ N, N보다, -아/어 보여요, -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같아요)
Integration 3: time and condition (-(으)ㄹ 때, -기 전에 / -(으)ㄴ 후에, -(으)면)
vocabulario: 수고했어요 (good work, thanks for your effort)
practica: Lab 2 '24 hours in Seoul' (15 minutes) in rooms of 3: each group builds a plan that includes a concert, a short trip, a meal, a photo in 한복 (traditional dress) and a PC방 (internet café) and sums it up in the chat in 3 sentences; it's a warm-up and isn't graded

Oral assessment in pairs (40 minutes, 5 minutes per pair): Abby drops into each room, draws the 3-minute role play (restaurant or travel agency) and asks each student 2 follow-up questions; while they wait, pairs keep talking with the station cards
Wrap-up (5 minutes): a round of 축하해요 (congratulations) and each student states in Korean one goal for Conversational 2; the individual report and the certificate arrive the following week
tarea: Before class: record the 2-minute monologue on the module you draw in the lottery on Sunday the 22nd (no reading; cue card with keywords only) and prepare both possible role plays
Re-record the week 1 self-introduction (now 2–3 minutes) and send it along with the original before class: it's your 'before and after' and part of the assessment
After class: complete the final self-assessment and the course survey; Abby returns the individual report along with the certificate
semanas.cultura: When finishing team work in Korea, people say 수고하셨습니다 (thank you for your effort): it acknowledges the other person's work, not just the result, and that same phrase closes every class.

evaluacion.quizzes: 5-minute oral quiz at the start of classes 2 through 7: five questions on the previous module (vocabulary and one structure), answered out loud or in the Zoom chat. It has no separate grade: it counts within the 40% participation and helps Abby decide what to reactivate in that day's practice room.
evaluacion.tareas: Each week 2–3 submissions (always a 60–120 second audio and a short written task) via the course WhatsApp group before the next class; Abby returns corrections by audio or text within 48 hours. They account for 30% of the overall grade; up to 2 late submissions are accepted without penalty.
evaluacion.examen_final: End-of-stage oral assessment, no written exam, in two parts. Before class 8, by audio: (1) extended self-introduction of 2–3 minutes (the week 1 one re-recorded); (2) 2-minute monologue on a module drawn the previous Sunday (K-pop, travel, food, 한복 (traditional dress) or e-sports). In class 8, in pairs with Abby in the room (5 minutes per pair): (3) 3-minute role play drawn between restaurant and travel agency; (4) two follow-up questions for each student. Rubric of 5 criteria at 20% each: fluency, accuracy of the course structures, module vocabulary, pronunciation and interaction (listening and reacting). Worth 30% of the overall grade; anyone who misses class 8 does the role play with Abby in a 10-minute Zoom appointment within the week.
evaluacion.oral: The course is 100% oral: 40% participation (quizzes, practice rooms and the two labs), 30% audio and written homework, 30% final oral assessment. The week 1 audio is re-recorded in week 8 as 'before and after' evidence of progress, is part of the final assessment and is discussed in the individual report.
evaluacion.certificado: Academia Seúl Certificate · Conversational 1 · CEFR A2.1 (partial) · TOPIK I level 2 preparation, issued November 30. Requirements: ≥ 60% overall grade and ≥ 75% attendance (6 of 8 live classes; the recording does not count as attendance unless notified in advance). Grants direct access to Conversational 2 (A2.2, January 2027) with no placement test.

materiales: Trilingual ES/KO/EN decks for modules M01–M05 (K-pop and fan culture, travel to Jeju and Seoul, food culture, 한복 (traditional dress) and aesthetics, PC방 (internet café) and e-sports), in-house template
Activity sheet per session (PDF) with vocabulary, module structures and the role play script
Station cards for the two labs (travel agency, restaurant, fan meetup, 24 hours in Seoul) and topic cards for the oral assessment
Grammar reference: Korean Grammar in Use · Beginning, cited by unit when a structure calls for it (not studied linearly)
Authentic material: real menus from Seoul restaurants, Seoul subway map, short clips from concerts and the LCK with subtitles
Zoom with breakout rooms and recording available 24 hours after each class
the course WhatsApp group group to submit audios, receive corrections and share discoveries between classes
Hangul Reader (Words and Time Trial tabs) as optional reading warm-up between sessions
notas_profesor: Students arrive from Basic 2 with the past and future still 'green': don't reteach them, reactivate them in context. If someone gets -았/었어요 (past) wrong, give the model in 10 seconds and move on with the topic; the spiral of the course ladder takes care of the rest.

Typical Spanish-speaker pronunciation: confuses ㅓ/ㅗ (서울 sounds like 소울) and ㅡ/ㅜ, softens the tense consonants ㄸ/ㄲ (떡볶이), doesn't assimilate the batchim ㄹ+ㄴ (한라산 is pronounced [할라산]) and pronounces ㄹ between vowels like a strong Spanish r (노래, 머리). Correct only one thing per turn, always with a model and repetition, never with a long explanation.

Most frequent structural errors: mixing up 좋아요 and 좋아해요 (BTS가 좋아해요), calquing the Spanish 'tener X años' (literally 'to have X years') with 있어요, placing the verb in the middle of the sentence and using -고 싶어요 in the third person. Note them in the chat while you rotate through the rooms and return them at wrap-up (delayed correction); never interrupt a monologue.

90/10 rule: Korean 90% of the time; ES/EN glosses live in the trilingual deck and in the Zoom chat, never in full-sentence translations. Abby doesn't need to speak Spanish: rephrasing, gesturing and showing the image works better and is part of the student's training.

Energy and pace: for the students it's 21:00 after work and for you it's 9:00 in the morning. Start with cameras on and the 10 minutes of 스몰토크 (small talk), call each student by name at least 3 times per class and don't let the deck run past 20 minutes: if the explanation grows, cut the explanation, not the practice.

Differentiation in the rooms: pair a strong student with an average one, never two strong ones together; hand a 'support card' with 3 model sentences to whoever freezes up and ask for an extra sentence with -지만 (but) or -는데 (soft contrast) from whoever is well ahead. In the labs, each room without the teacher has a designated leader who hands out turns and keeps time.

Diagnostic and assessment: in week 1 note 3 data points per student on the group sheet (fluency, pronunciation, personal goal) while you rotate through the rooms; in week 8 listen to the audios (the 'before and after' self-introduction and the monologue) before class, so that only the pair role play remains live, and apply the 5-criteria rubric. With ≥ 60% and 6 of 8 attendances the certificate is issued; offer anyone on the borderline a make-up oral task with a 7-day deadline.

descripcion: Small group (maximum 8) focused 100% on the official TOPIK II exam: strategy by section — 듣기 (listening), 쓰기 (writing) and 읽기 (reading) —, personalized writing correction every week and timed mock exams with official past papers. TOPIK II is a single exam that awards levels 3 through 6 depending on your score (out of 300): here you learn to lock in the profitable points, stop giving away time and write formats 51–54 with templates that work. Ideal if you are aiming for the April 2027 TOPIK.
perfil_alumno: Adults with intermediate Korean (B1): you understand everyday dialogues and texts, write connected paragraphs and handle connectors such as -아/어서, -지만 and -(으)니까. You are going to take TOPIK II for university, work, a visa, a scholarship or a personal goal, and you want a concrete plan instead of studying blindly. It also works if you have already taken the exam and fell just a few points short of level 3 or 4. Group of at most 8 students so that 쓰기 (writing) correction can be individual and line by line.
requisito_entrada: Intermediate level (B1), one step above the last course of the Academia Seúl ladder (Conversational 2, A2.2): demonstrated with the placement test (TOPIK-style written diagnostic + 5-minute conversation with Jay) or with a previous TOPIK result. Class 1 confirms placement with a diagnostic mock exam; if the result shows gaps in the fundamentals (0 of 3 connectors correct or unable to write question 51), Conversational 1 (A2.1) or Conversational 2 (A2.2) is honestly recommended before this course.
objetivos: Master the strategy for each section of the exam: which questions to attack first, which to skip and how to manage the 180 minutes (듣기 60 · 쓰기 50 · 읽기 70).

Write the four 쓰기 formats (51, 52, 53 and 54) with proven templates and the right register for each one (-(스)ㅂ니다 in 51, the written style -(느)ㄴ다 in 52–54), with personal correction from the teacher every week.
Solve 듣기 and 읽기 1–20 with at least 70% accuracy and pick up points on level 4–6 questions through inference, sequencing and the speaker's attitude.
Take a full timed mock exam with an official past paper and read your score against the official cutoffs (level 3: 120 · level 4: 150 · level 5: 190 · level 6: 230).
Take in more than 90 high-frequency exam words (economy, society, environment, surveys, opinion) by using them in your own writing.
Leave with a personal, weekly and realistic study plan through the April 2027 TOPIK, with the registration date and test site identified.

estructura_clase.detalle: Five TOPIK-style questions on the previous week's vocabulary and strategy; times and scores from the timed homework are reviewed.
Jay breaks down the day's question type or 쓰기 format with an official past paper on screen: the pattern, the typical trap and the formula that earns points.
Live solving with a visible timer (individually or in pairs), immediate correction and point tally; in 쓰기 weeks, a guided writing workshop with the rubric.
On-screen review of two or three pieces of homework (anonymous): what earned points, what lost them and how to say it in written style.
Summary of the day's formula, the week's timed homework and a score target for the next class.

semanas.leccion: Anatomy of the exam (sections, timing, scoring and level cutoffs) + a reduced diagnostic mock taken from a published official past paper: 읽기 1–10, 쓰기 51 and 듣기 1–10, plus an individual oral interview. Materials: Academia Seúl strategy guide (class 1) and an official past paper from topik.go.kr.
semanas.objetivo: Know the structure and scoring of TOPIK II, set your target date and know, with data, your starting level in each section.
gramatica: Anatomy: 듣기 (listening) 50 questions · 60 min · 쓰기 (writing) 4 questions · 50 min · 읽기 (reading) 50 questions · 70 min; levels 3–6 depending on the score out of 300 (cutoffs 120 / 150 / 190 / 230)
Golden rule: never leave an answer blank (there is no penalty for wrong answers) and never get stuck in 듣기: questions 1–20 are played only once and 21–50 twice
The three connectors in the diagnostic that place your starting level: -(으)니까 (reason, in contrast with -아/어서), -지만 (contrast) and -기 위해서 (purpose)
practica: Timed diagnostic mock: 읽기 1–10 and 쓰기 51 in 15 silent minutes, then 듣기 1–10 with the official audio (8 minutes); immediate correction and a point tally per student

2-minute 1:1 diagnostic interview in a breakout room, while the others solve the written part: why you are taking TOPIK, your target date and reading a short paragraph aloud to measure fluency and vocabulary
Live calculation of 'my score today → my target cutoff': each student places their result on the level 3–6 table and defines how many points they need per section
tarea: Memorize the 12 words and write 2 sentences with each verb (증가하다, 감소하다, 해결하다); send the text in the course WhatsApp group before Thursday
Solve 읽기 1–20 from an official past paper in 20 timed minutes and note how long each question took you
Listen to 15 minutes of a slow Korean podcast (options via WhatsApp) and note 5 new words; optional: 10 minutes a day on the Hangul Reader in Time Trial mode for reading speed
semanas.cultura: TOPIK is administered by the 국립국제교육원 (National Institute for International Education of Korea) and in Latin America it is taken at authorized sites at embassies and Korean Cultural Centers; level 3 opens doors to universities and scholarships, and level 4 is the one many employers ask for.

semanas.leccion: 읽기 1–20 from the official past paper, type by type: 1–2 grammar in context, 3–4 expression with an equivalent meaning, 5–8 what the notice is about, 9–12 matching a text or graph, 13–15 ordering four sentences, 16–18 fill in the blank and 19–20 short text with a connector and main idea. Typical traps and the clock: the exam allows about 80 seconds per question on average, but the first 20 should take under 45 seconds each to save time for the hard ones.
semanas.objetivo: Solve 읽기 1–20 in under 15 minutes with at least 70% accuracy, recognizing each question type before reading the full text.
gramatica: -자마자 (as soon as…) and -(으)ㄹ수록 (the more…): the most frequent connectors in 읽기 1–2
-기 마련이다 ≈ -는 법이다 (it is natural that…) and -(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다 ≈ -아/어야 하다 (there is no choice but to…): equivalent pairs for 읽기 3–4
Sequencing words (읽기 13–15): 그런데 (but), 그래서 (so, therefore), 이처럼 (like this, in this way), 또한 (also, in addition) as sequence clues
Speed-reading notices (읽기 5–8): read only the key nouns, not the whole sentence
practica: Race against the clock in pairs: 읽기 1–8 in 4 minutes; then each pair explains in Korean why they ruled out the other three options
Live ordering (읽기 13–15): the four sentences are handed out among the students and the group negotiates the order aloud before seeing the answer
Guided annotation on screen: how to mark the key words in the prompt and the 'trap' in each wrong option in 읽기 9–12
tarea: 읽기 1–20 from two different official past papers, timed (15 minutes each); send your answer sheet and total time
Written card of 10 equivalent expressions (읽기 3–4) with your own example for each one
1-minute audio reading a 읽기 5–8 notice aloud: pronunciation and rhythm correction via WhatsApp
semanas.cultura: The notices in 읽기 5–8 are the ones from real Korean life: 분리수거 (sorting recyclables), 에너지 절약 (energy-saving) campaigns and 동아리 (university clubs); knowing that context is worth points and does not require reading the whole sentence.

semanas.leccion: 듣기 1–20 from the official past paper: 1–3 choosing the picture or graph, 4–8 the next line in the dialogue, 9–12 what the person will do next, 13–16 content matching and 17–20 the man's main idea. Minimal note-taking technique with symbols and reading the options before the audio starts.
semanas.objetivo: Solve 듣기 1–20 on a single listen, reading the options before the audio and taking two- or three-word notes per question.
gramatica: -(으)ㄹ게요 / -(으)ㄹ까요? (commitment and suggestion): the typical replies in 듣기 4–8
-아/어 주시겠어요? and -(으)면 안 될까요? (polite requests that signal the next action in 듣기 9–12)
-는 게 좋겠어요 / -아/어야죠 (the speaker's opinion and advice): the key to 듣기 17–20
Symbol notes while you listen: ↑↓ (increases / decreases), ♂ / ♀ (man / woman), ✓ / ✗ (agrees / disagrees)
practica: Active dictation: the teacher plays a 듣기 4–8 dialogue in three segments; each student writes down the last line and proposes the reply before seeing the options
Role play in pairs with a 듣기 9–12 script (customer and employee): the partner guesses in Korean 'what the woman or the man will do now'
Mini mock 듣기 1–12 with official audio (about 12 minutes) and a live tally of correct answers
tarea: 듣기 1–20 from an official past paper at home, one listen only and no pausing; then a second listen with the 대본 (script), marking the words you missed
2-minute audio summarizing a 듣기 13–16 dialogue in Korean, in your own words
5 minutes of shadowing a day with the official audio: repeat aloud 3 seconds behind the speaker
semanas.cultura: In the exam dialogues the man and the woman are usually 동료 (colleagues) or 선배/후배 (senior and junior): the -(으)세요 register versus -(스)ㅂ니다 reveals who ranks higher, and listening for that tone helps you guess the answer.

semanas.leccion: 쓰기 51 (practical text: notice, email, invitation or message) and 쓰기 52 (short explanatory text): two blanks ㉠ and ㉡ worth 5 points each, 20 points in total. High-frequency formulas, the correct register for each text and the grading criteria (content, grammar and register). Official past papers + our own templates.
semanas.objetivo: Score between 15 and 20 of the 20 points in 쓰기 51–52 with safe formulas and the right register for each type of text.
gramatica: -(으)려고 합니다 / -고 싶습니다 (intention: 'I want to / we are going to…') for blank ㉠ of 51
-아/어 주시기 바랍니다 / -(으)시면 됩니다 (formal request in notices and emails) for blank ㉡ of 51
-기 때문이다 / -아/어야 한다 in the written style -(느)ㄴ다 (cause and obligation in 52)
Logical connectors for 52: 그러므로 (therefore), 그러나 (however), 왜냐하면 (because), 반면에 (on the other hand)
practica: Live correction of 51 answers from the homework (anonymous, on screen): the group scores them 0 to 5 with the rubric and compares with the teacher's judgment
Register-switching workshop in pairs: the same sentence in -아/어요, -(스)ㅂ니다 and -(느)ㄴ다 (written style) against the clock
Two new 51s and two new 52s in 12 minutes, individually, with immediate correction and point tally
tarea: Solve 쓰기 51–52 from three official past papers by hand (photo of the sheet): personal correction from the teacher before class 5
Written list of 15 formulas for 51–52 in Hangul with your own translation, to memorize
Rewrite a real message you sent this week on WhatsApp as a 3-line Korean practical text, using -기 바랍니다 twice
semanas.cultura: The 쓰기 51 texts imitate real notices from 아파트 (apartment buildings) and 동아리 (university clubs): there they are always written in -(스)ㅂ니다, because in Korea a public notice keeps a polite distance even among neighbors.

semanas.leccion: 쓰기 53 (30 points): describing a survey or graph in 200–300 characters with the 4-sentence template (who, whom and about what → main result and runner-up → comparison or change over time → cause or projection). Rules of the 원고지 (grid sheet): one character per box, indentation and punctuation marks. Graphs from official past papers.
semanas.objetivo: Write a complete 53 in 15 minutes, with no template or 원고지 errors, and score at least 20 of the 30 points.
gramatica: -을/를 대상으로 -에 대해 조사를 실시하였다 (sentence 1: who surveyed, whom and about what)
-이/가 -%로 가장 높게 나타났고, -이/가 그 뒤를 이었다 (sentence 2: main result and second place)
-에서 -(으)로 증가하였다 / 감소하였다 · N배 늘었다 (sentence 3: change between two years or two groups)
-(으)ㄹ 것으로 전망된다 / -기 때문인 것으로 보인다 (sentence 4: projection or cause)
practica: Guided construction of a 53 on a shared whiteboard: the group dictates sentences 1 to 4 about an official graph and the teacher writes on a digital 원고지, counting characters aloud
Peer correction in pairs with the official rubric (content and task, structure, language use): each pair scores the other's 53 and justifies it in Korean
Individual time trial: a new 53 in 15 minutes, sent by photo, with a brief comment from the teacher for each student at the end
tarea: Two 53s from official past papers handwritten on 원고지 (photo): personal line-by-line correction from the teacher before class 6
Find a real graph from a Korean newspaper (연합뉴스 or 통계청) and describe it in 4 sentences with the template; post it in the course WhatsApp group
Memorize the 4 template sentences and record yourself reciting them from memory (1-minute audio)
semanas.cultura: The 53 graphs come from real surveys by 통계청 (Statistics Korea) and institutes like 한국갤럽 (Gallup Korea); the recurring topics —birth rate, youth employment, smartphone use— are the conversations of today's Korea.

semanas.leccion: Second half of both sections with official past papers. 읽기 21–50: idiomatic expressions and main idea (21–22), the character's mood (23–24), news headlines (25–27), fill in the blank (28–31), topic of the text (35–38), where the sentence goes (39–41) and the author's attitude and purpose (46–50). 듣기 21–50: interviews (25–26), the speaker's intention (27–28), who is speaking (29–30), debate and attitude (31–32, 45–50). Triage strategy: what to skip and what to come back to.
semanas.objetivo: Add 15 to 20 extra points in the second half of each section without giving away time: identify the question type, attack the profitable ones and leave the level 6 questions for last.
gramatica: Headlines (읽기 25–27): nominalized style with no conjugated verb — 급증 (sharp increase), 전망 (outlook), 잇따라 (one after another)
-(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다 (amounts to…), -(으)ㄹ 따름이다 (nothing more than…), -(으)ㄴ/는 반면에 (whereas…): level 4–5 nuances that fill the blanks in 읽기 28–31
Attitude verbs for 읽기 46–50 and 듣기 45–50: 우려하다 (to be concerned), 비판하다 (to criticize), 동의하다 (to agree), 기대하다 (to expect, to look forward to)
Cohesion clues for 읽기 39–41: 이는 (this), 그러한 (such), 이에 따라 (accordingly), 예를 들어 (for example)
practica: Triage in pairs: 10 mixed questions from 읽기 21–50, 2 minutes to sort them into 'now', 'later' or 'guess' and defend the criteria
Live headlines (읽기 25–27): each student rebuilds a headline as a full sentence in Korean and the group picks the option
Simulated debate from 듣기 31–32: two students read a short debate script, the rest identify each speaker's 태도 (attitude) and 의도 (intention)
tarea: 읽기 21–50 from an official past paper in 50 timed minutes, skipping around as in the real exam, plus a triage sheet with what you skipped and why
듣기 21–50 at home with two listens per question, as in the real exam, and no pausing; then a 2-minute audio explaining in Korean the speaker's attitude in two questions from 45–50
Written card of 15 headlines from 읽기 25–27 with their 'de-nominalized' version as a full sentence
semanas.cultura: Level 5–6 texts cite Korea's history and social debates: 조선 (the Joseon dynasty), 세종대왕 (King Sejong, creator of Hangul) and 저출산 (low birth rate) come up again and again; reading one 연합뉴스 headline a day trains exactly that.

semanas.leccion: 쓰기 54 (50 points): opinion essay of 600–700 characters based on a topic and two or three guiding questions. The template: 서론 (introduction: importance of the topic) → 본론 (two paragraphs answering the guiding questions) → 결론 (conclusion with a stance). Written style -(느)ㄴ다, with no spoken-language markers. Topics from recent official past papers + personal correction.
semanas.objetivo: Produce a complete, coherent 54 in 30 minutes, answering the guiding questions and scoring at least 25 of the 50 rubric points.
gramatica: -(으)ㄴ/는 것이 중요하다 / -(으)ㄹ 필요가 있다 (stating importance and necessity in the introduction)
첫째 · 둘째 · 마지막으로 + -기 때문이다 (ordering and justifying reasons in the body)
-(으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 (not only… but also) · -(으)ㅁ으로써 (by means of) · -(으)ㄹ 수 있도록 (so that one can): academic-register connectors
따라서 (therefore) · 이처럼 (in this way) · -아/어야 할 것이다 (will have to…): the conclusion's closing with a stance
practica: Timed brainstorm (5 minutes) on a recent official topic: each student writes down two reasons and one example in Korean and presents them in 30 seconds
Collaborative building of the essay skeleton on a shared whiteboard: one sentence per student; the teacher corrects the register (-아/어요 → -(느)ㄴ다) live
Correction clinic: two essays from the homework (anonymous) projected on screen; the group points out three strengths and three improvements using the rubric
tarea: One complete 54 handwritten on 원고지 on the topic given in class (30 timed minutes, photo): personal line-by-line correction from the teacher before the mock exam
Rewrite the same essay applying the corrections and record yourself reading it aloud (3-minute audio)
Personal bank of 20 ready-to-use opinion expressions (Hangul + gloss in Spanish), shared in the course WhatsApp group
semanas.cultura: The 54 topics reflect the debates Korea has with itself: 경쟁 사회 (competitive society), 인공지능 (artificial intelligence), 환경 (environment); graders reward a balanced, well-structured stance more than a controversial opinion.

semanas.leccion: Full timed exam with an unseen official past paper, taken at home between class 7 and class 8 (듣기 50 questions · 60 min, 쓰기 4 questions · 50 min, 읽기 50 questions · 70 min; 180 minutes with the official answer sheet). In class: section-by-section analysis, surprise mini mock, reading your score against the cutoffs and building your personal plan through the real TOPIK.
semanas.objetivo: Finish with a real score out of 300, know what level you are at today and leave with a weekly study plan through the April 2027 TOPIK.
gramatica: Reading your score: cutoffs 120 / 150 / 190 / 230 and how many points you are missing per section for your target level
Time management on the real exam: 듣기 60' without pausing · 쓰기 50' (51–52 in 8', 53 in 15', 54 in 27') · 읽기 70' (1–25 in 25 minutes)
Spaced study plan: one full official past paper a month, two 쓰기 sessions a week and 15 minutes of 듣기 a day
Exam logistics: registration on topik.go.kr during the window published by your country's test site (for April it usually opens early in the year), documents and what to bring on exam day
practica: 3-minute individual review per student of the full mock exam (while the others adjust their plan): score by section, level reached and the three question types that cost them the most points
10-minute surprise mini mock (듣기 5 questions + 읽기 5) to measure reflexes under pressure after seven weeks
Each student presents in 1 minute, in Korean, their goal (target level and date) and their weekly plan; wrap-up with certificate delivery
tarea: Before class: take the full 180-minute mock exam with an official past paper you have not seen, timer in view and the official answer sheet; send the sheet and the scanned 쓰기
After class: write your weekly study plan through April 2027 in Korean (150 characters) and post it in the course WhatsApp group
Mark the registration period for the April 2027 TOPIK on topik.go.kr in your calendar and confirm your country's test site
semanas.cultura: Exam day in Korea is almost a ritual: 수험표 (admission slip) and 신분증 (ID card) in hand, phone off, and many bring 엿 (malt taffy) or 찹쌀떡 (glutinous rice cake) to 'stick' to a pass, because 붙다 means both to stick and to pass.

evaluacion.quizzes: 5-minute quiz at the start of each class (weeks 2 to 8): five TOPIK-style questions on the previous week's strategy and vocabulary, corrected live. Worth 20% of the final grade.
evaluacion.tareas: One timed homework assignment per week (one section of an official past paper plus a written or audio production), submitted via the course WhatsApp group before the next class. 쓰기 assignments receive personal line-by-line correction from the teacher. Worth 30% of the final grade.
evaluacion.examen_final: Full TOPIK II mock exam with an unseen official past paper, taken timed at home between classes 7 and 8: 듣기 50 questions in 60 minutes, 쓰기 4 questions (51–54) in 50 minutes and 읽기 50 questions in 70 minutes; 180 minutes in total, with the official answer sheet. Graded with the official answer key and the 쓰기 rubric and converted into an estimated level (3–6). Plus a 10-minute mini mock in class 8. Worth 40% of the final grade.
evaluacion.oral: TOPIK II has no speaking section, but the course assesses it anyway: individual diagnostic interview in class 1 (ungraded), participation in role plays, active dictations and simulated debates, and a final 1-minute presentation in Korean of your goal and study plan in class 8. Worth 10% of the final grade.
evaluacion.certificado: Academia Seúl certificate 'TOPIK II Preparation · CEFR B1+' with the final mock exam score and the estimated TOPIK level (3–6), issued the week of November 30, 2026. Requirements: overall grade of at least 60%, attendance of at least 75% (6 of the 8 live classes; watching the recording does not count as attendance) and submission of the full mock exam. The official TOPIK certificate is issued only by the 국립국제교육원 (National Institute for International Education) upon taking the real exam.

materiales: Official published TOPIK II past papers (기출문제) from topik.go.kr, with audio and answer keys: four or five different papers are used during the course
Academia Seúl's own strategy materials: guide by question type, 쓰기 51–54 templates and grading rubrics explained in Spanish
Printable official answer sheet (답안지) and 원고지 (grid sheet) to practice 쓰기 by hand, as in the real exam
Visible timer in every practice session (on Zoom and on the student's phone)
Korean Grammar in Use · Intermediate (Darakwon) as an optional reference for level 3–4 patterns; not studied linearly
Course the course WhatsApp group group: homework submission, shared expression bank and questions between classes; recording of each class available 24 hours later
Hangul Reader (Time Trial mode) as an optional reading-speed warm-up
Slow Korean podcasts and 연합뉴스 (Yonhap News Agency) headlines as recommended daily input
notas_profesor: Honest diagnostic in class 1: if a student scores 0 of 3 on the connectors or cannot write question 51, suggest Conversational 1 (A2.1) or Conversational 2 (A2.2) instead of this course; better a student happy at their level than frustrated in TOPIK II. If they score 3 of 3 and write natural sentences, move them up to the 54 from week 5.

Typical mistake of Spanish speakers in 쓰기: writing in the spoken register (-아/어요) where the written style -(느)ㄴ다 belongs, and translating 'because' with 왜냐하면 without closing the sentence with -기 때문이다. Always correct these two; let spacing and minor spelling slide in 51–52.

In 듣기 students get stuck on the previous question and miss the next one: explicitly train 'let go and move on'. They also confuse the male and female voices when the question asks for the idea of the 남자 (man): have them mark ♂ / ♀ on the sheet before the audio starts.

Pacing: the class only pays off if the timed practice really lasts 25 minutes with a visible timer; do not run long on the strategy explanation. Detailed 쓰기 correction goes in writing between classes, not live (live, only two or three anonymous cases).

Differentiation with 8 students: set up two sub-goals (level 3 and level 4–5). The level 3 group works 읽기 and 듣기 1–25 and 쓰기 51–53 to perfection; the 4–5 group adds 읽기 35–50, 듣기 41–50 and the full 54. Same homework, different threshold.

Vocabulary: do not hand out long lists; 12 words a week with the obligation to use them in the written homework. Reinforce the pairs 증가 / 감소 (increase / decrease), 긍정적 / 부정적 (positive / negative) and 장점 / 단점 (advantage / disadvantage): they show up in the 53 and 54 of almost every exam.

Watch morale in week 6: scores usually drop because the questions are harder. Remind them that level 3 is 40% of the exam and that level 6 questions are not their goal. Celebrate the points gained in 쓰기, which is where you climb the most in 8 weeks.

nombre: Korean for Kids (8–12) · Play and Learn
descripcion: Korean from scratch for kids ages 8 to 12, with games, songs and drawings. In 8 live 60-minute Zoom classes with two native teachers, they learn to read 한글 (the Korean alphabet), introduce themselves with their name and age, count from 1 to 10, and name animals, family members and Korean foods. The activity changes every 8–10 minutes to keep their attention, and every week the family receives a note with what to review in the Hangul Reader. Closing: a mini-show in Korean for the families and a certificate.
perfil_alumno: Boys and girls ages 8 to 12, Spanish speakers, with no prior knowledge of Korean (or just a few loose words from K-pop and dramas). Curious, eager to play, sing and draw, and with an adult at home who can support the 20 minutes of homework and receive the weekly note via WhatsApp. Ideal if K-dramas or K-pop are part of life at home and the child wants to "understand what they're saying."
requisito_entrada: None: we start from absolute zero. Practical requirements: be between 8 and 12 years old, a computer or tablet with camera and microphone, a quiet spot during class, paper and colored pencils on hand, and a responsible adult who manages the family's WhatsApp (sending homework, receiving the weekly note and giving permission for the final show).
objetivos: Read simple syllables and words in 한글 (Korean alphabet) aloud: basic vowels and consonants and the most common batchim.
Say hello, goodbye and thank you in Korean with the appropriate little bow.
Introduce themselves with name and age: 안녕하세요, 저는 ___이에요/예요, ___ 살이에요.
Count from 1 to 10 with native Korean numbers and ask someone's age.
Name 10 animals, family members and 10 Korean foods, and say which ones they like and don't like.
Write their own name and short words in 한글.
Give a 30–40-second mini-show in Korean for their family and receive their certificate.

estructura_clase.detalle: 안녕하세요 greeting with a bow, song of the week and roll call as a game: each child answers 네 (yes) and shows the week's drawing or homework to the camera.
5-minute quiz game on the previous class (bingo, memory or 'Jay Says') and lightning review of the Hangul Reader homework; progress-board stickers are handed out.

Two 10-minute mini-blocks with a change of activity: Jay presents the content with drawings, gestures and real objects; then Abby leads a movement game (total physical response) to lock it in with body and voice.
Two Zoom breakout rooms of up to 6 kids, one with Jay and one with Abby: drawing, building syllables, role play, reading bingo or pair interviews; one-on-one pronunciation correction.

estructura_clase.bloque: Wrap-up and note to the family
estructura_clase.detalle: Goodbye song, sticker of the day and explanation of the homework with the exact Hangul Reader tab. After class, the family receives the weekly note via WhatsApp.

semanas.leccion: Greetings with songs + first vowels through play. First class: getting to know each other, learning to greet with a bow, and discovering the 6 basic vowels with body, voice and the Hangul Reader.
semanas.objetivo: Say hello, goodbye and thank you in Korean, answer 네 / 아니요 in games, and recognize and read the 6 basic vowels ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ.
gramatica: 안녕하세요 (hello) · 안녕 (hi / bye, between friends) — fixed phrases with a bow, no analysis
네 (yes) / 아니요 (no) — for answering roll call and games
Basic vowels ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ with the silent ㅇ at the start: 아 어 오 우 으 이
vocabulario: 안녕히 계세요 (goodbye, when you are the one leaving)
practica: 안녕 greeting song with gestures and a slight bow; repeated faster and faster until everyone sings it from memory.
'Living vowel' game: Jay shows a vowel and the kids make its shape with their arms (ㅏ arm to the right, ㅗ arm up, ㅡ arms open wide); then in reverse, one child poses and the others guess.
Vowel bingo with audio: Abby pronounces a vowel and the kids mark it on their 6-square card; whoever completes a row reads it aloud.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Alphabet tab: tap and repeat the 6 vowels aloud (5 minutes, on 3 different days), then Practice → Vowels until 10 correct answers.
Color the 6-vowel worksheet (comes with the weekly note) and stick it up near the computer.
Record a 10-second audio with 안녕하세요 and 감사합니다 and send it through the family WhatsApp.
semanas.cultura: In Korea, people greet with a small bow (인사 = greeting); the kids practice it in the song and use it when entering and leaving every class.

semanas.leccion: Basic consonants + everyone writes their name in 한글. We discover the first 10 consonants, learn to build our first syllable, and each child takes home their name written in Korean.
semanas.objetivo: Recognize the basic consonants ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ, read simple consonant + vowel syllables, write their own name in 한글 and introduce themselves with it.
gramatica: 저는 ___이에요/예요 (I am ___) — set phrase for introducing yourself by name
이름이 뭐예요? (what's your name?) — fixed question passed around the circle
Consonant + vowel = syllable: ㄱ + ㅏ = 가; ㄴ + ㅏ = 나 (the factory starts running)
practica: Each child builds their name with letter cards on the Zoom whiteboard while Jay guides the transcription (Sofía → 소피아, Mateo → 마테오, Valentina → 발렌티나); then writes it on a big sheet of paper and shows it to the camera.
'이름이 뭐예요?' round: in a virtual circle, each child asks the next one, who answers 저는 ___이에요/예요; Abby corrects the bow and intonation.
Drawn dictation: Abby says 나무 or 바다, the kids have 20 seconds to draw what they heard and write the word underneath.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Alphabet: consonants (tap and repeat) and Practice → Consonants until 10 correct answers.
Decorate the sheet with your name in 한글 (colors, drawings, stickers): we'll show it at the start of next class and it will be part of the final show.
10-second audio: 안녕하세요, 저는 ___이에요/예요.
semanas.cultura: October 9 is 한글날 (Hangul Day), a public holiday in Korea: it celebrates the alphabet that King 세종대왕 (King Sejong the Great) invented so everyone could learn to read, and this week every child is already writing their name with it.

semanas.leccion: Building and reading syllables + reading bingo. We turn letters into syllables and syllables into real words, and the 받침 (final consonant) shows up in very common words.
semanas.objetivo: Combine consonant + vowel to read any simple syllable, recognize the batchim ㄴ, ㅁ, ㅇ, ㄹ in short words, and read 10 one- and two-syllable words aloud.
gramatica: The syllable as a block: consonant + vowel (가) and consonant + vowel + 받침 (강)
Most common 받침 (final consonant): ㄴ, ㅁ, ㅇ, ㄹ — just recognize and read, no rules
ㅇ has two faces: silent at the start (아) and an 'ng' sound at the end (강)
practica: Syllable factory: Jay fixes a consonant on the whiteboard and the kids 'manufacture' syllables by changing the vowel in chorus (가 거 고 구 그 기); then a child picks the consonant and runs the factory.
Reading bingo: a 9-syllable card per child; Abby reads one syllable every 10 seconds and they mark it; the winner reads their full row aloud.
Batchim race: in teams of 3, each team reads 5 words with 받침 as fast as possible while Jay and Abby time them and correct the final ㅇ.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Learn: Syllables and Batchim; then Practice → Syllables (10 correct) and Batchim (10 correct).
한글 hunters: find 3 Korean words around the house (a ramen package, a K-pop album, a drama on TV) and send a photo or drawing of one.
Audio: read the 11 words of the week aloud.
semanas.cultura: Korean syllables are written in square blocks, as if each one lived in a little box; that's why an old book says a clever person can learn 한글 in a single morning.

semanas.leccion: 10 animals + 'it's a…!' (이에요/예요) with drawings. First real structure: saying what something is. The animals arrive with sounds, gestures and lightning drawings.
semanas.objetivo: Name 10 animals, ask 이거 뭐예요? and answer ___이에요/예요, and present their favorite animal with a drawing.
gramatica: N + 이에요/예요 (it's a ___): 곰이에요 after a consonant, 토끼예요 after a vowel
이거 뭐예요? (what is this?) — question and answer in game format
Korean animal onomatopoeia: 멍멍 (woof), 야옹 (meow), 꿀꿀 (oink) — for laughs and to lock in the sound
practica: Guess the animal: Abby makes the sound or gesture and the kids shout the full answer: 호랑이예요!; the first to get it right does the next one.
Lightning drawing: in 30 seconds they draw the animal Jay names, show it to the camera and say 이거 곰이에요; Jay corrects 이에요 / 예요 with a gesture (fist = consonant, open hand = vowel).
On-screen memory game: 12 cards with drawings and words in 한글; the child who finds the pair reads it aloud and answers 이거 뭐예요?
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Words and Pictograms: read 15 words with pictures (send a screenshot of your progress).
Draw your favorite animal and write its name in 한글: you'll present it in 10 seconds next class and it goes into the final show.
Audio: 3 sentences 이거 ___이에요/예요 with your stuffed animals or the pets at home.
semanas.cultura: The 호랑이 (tiger) is Korea's symbolic animal: it stars in ancient tales, was the mascot of the 1988 Seoul Olympics and is the seal of Academia Seúl.

semanas.leccion: 엄마, 아빠, 할머니… introducing the family with a photo or drawing. Each child brings a photo or drawing of their family and learns to introduce them in Korean.
semanas.objetivo: Name family members and introduce 2 or 3 people with a photo or drawing: 이 사람은 우리 엄마예요.
gramatica: 우리 + family member (우리 엄마 = my mom) — in Korean, family is always 'ours'
이 사람은 ___이에요/예요 (this person is ___) — review of 이에요/예요 with people
이름이 뭐예요? applied to a relative: 엄마 이름이 뭐예요? (what's your mom's name?)
vocabulario: 언니 (older sister, if you're a girl)
오빠 (older brother, if you're a girl)
누나 (older sister, if you're a boy)
형 (older brother, if you're a boy)
practica: Family show & tell: each child shows their photo or drawing and introduces 2 people with 이 사람은 우리 아빠예요; Abby models it first with a photo of her family in Korea.
Giant family tree: Jay shares an empty tree on the whiteboard and the kids say who goes on each branch (할머니 at the top, 동생 at the bottom) while a volunteer writes it in.
Family song with gestures (엄마, 아빠, 할머니, 할아버지…) at increasing speed; the last one to slip up picks the next song.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Words (10 correct) and one review round in Alphabet (vowels and consonants aloud).
Draw your family tree with the names in 한글 (at least 4 people; pets count too): it will be part of the final show.
Audio: introduce 3 people from your family with 이 사람은 우리 ___이에요/예요.
semanas.cultura: In Korea, older friends are also called 언니, 오빠, 누나 or 형, as if they were family; that's why you hear it so much in K-pop and dramas.

semanas.leccion: Counting from 1 to 10 + saying your age. Native Korean numbers with claps, jumps and a song, plus the most important question among Korean kids: how old are you?
semanas.objetivo: Count from 1 to 10 with native Korean numbers, ask 몇 살이에요? and say their own age: 저는 열 살이에요 (열한 / 열두 살 for the older kids).
gramatica: Native numbers 하나–열 (1–10): the ones used for counting things and saying your age
___ 살이에요 (I am ___ years old) with the short forms 한, 두, 세, 네 before 살; 11- and 12-year-olds say 열한 살, 열두 살
몇 살이에요? (how old are you?) — fixed question for the interview
practica: Numbers song with one clap per number and a jump on 열; then we sing it backwards (열, 아홉, 여덟…) and finally with gestures only, no voice.
'Jay Says / Abby Says': 셋! → everyone shows 3 fingers; 일곱! → 7 jumps; whoever slips up sits down and counts in Korean for those still playing.
Breakout-room interview: in pairs, 몇 살이에요? — 저는 아홉 살이에요; then each child reports their partner's age to the group (마테오는 열 살이에요).
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Numbers (native numbers round, 10 correct) and one try at the ⚡ Syllable Time Trial: send a screenshot of your time.
Count 10 objects in your home in Korean (pencils, spoons, stuffed animals) and record the audio up to 열.
Ask 2 people in your family their age in Korean and write down the answer with Korean numbers (you can use the cards from the weekly note).
semanas.cultura: On a Korean baby's first birthday, the 돌 (first birthday), there's the 돌잡이: the baby picks an object from a table (a pencil, a thread, money) that 'predicts' their future.

semanas.leccion: 김밥, 라면, 불고기 + 'I like' (좋아해요). Food week: we name Korean dishes, say what we like and don't like, and start rehearsing the final show script.
semanas.objetivo: Name 10 Korean foods and say which ones you like and don't like: 저는 김밥 좋아해요 / 김치 안 좋아해요; react with 맛있어요 or 매워요.
gramatica: N + 좋아해요 (I like ___): 김밥 좋아해요 — the particle 을/를 is only heard in the model, not explained
안 좋아해요 (I don't like) — the most useful negation in the course
뭐 좋아해요? (what do you like?) and the table reactions 맛있어요 (it's delicious!) / 매워요 (it's spicy)
practica: Drawing menu: each child draws their favorite Korean dish, shows it and presents it: 저는 떡볶이 좋아해요. 맛있어요!; Abby tells them what she ate today in Korea.
Lightning survey: Abby asks 김치 좋아해요? and the kids answer with a thumbs up or down plus the full sentence 네, 좋아해요 / 아니요, 안 좋아해요; Jay writes the group ranking on the whiteboard.
Guess the food: Jay shows a covered photo and uncovers it little by little; the first to name it in Korean wins a sticker and asks the next child 뭐 좋아해요?
tarea: Hangul Reader → Practice → Words and Pictograms (10 correct) and ⚡ Time Trial: try to beat last week's time.
Rehearse the final show script with the template from the weekly note (greeting, name, age, family, favorite animal and food; 30–40 seconds) and send a first test video.
Audio or video: try a Korean food (or show a photo of one) and say 맛있어요 or 매워요.
semanas.cultura: 김치 is eaten with almost every Korean meal, and in November families get together for 김장 (making kimchi for the whole winter), which UNESCO recognizes as cultural heritage.

semanas.leccion: Mini-presentation in Korean for the families + certificate. Families join the Zoom, each child presents their 30–40-second show, reads 5 words in 한글 and receives their certificate on screen.
semanas.objetivo: Introduce themselves in Korean for 30–40 seconds in front of their family (greeting, name, age, family, favorite animal and food), read 5 words in 한글 aloud and close with 감사합니다.
gramatica: Putting the script together: 안녕하세요 → 저는 ___이에요/예요 → ___ 살이에요 → 이 사람은 우리 ___이에요/예요 → 저는 ___ 좋아해요
Closing phrases: 감사합니다 (thank you) and 안녕히 계세요 (goodbye, when you are the one leaving) with a bow
vocabulario: 화이팅 (you can do it! / let's go!)
practica: Dress rehearsal in breakout rooms (first 15 minutes, before the families join): each child presents their script to Jay or Abby and gets one last gentle pronunciation correction.
Final show with the families on Zoom: each child presents for 30–40 seconds with their name sheet, family tree and animal; the others clap with 박수 and shout 잘했어요.
Closing ceremony: certificates presented on screen one by one with 축하해요, group photo with the 손하트 (finger heart) and goodbye with 안녕히 계세요.
tarea: Hangul Reader → Progress tab: send a screenshot of your progress (vowels, consonants, syllables, words) for the child's portfolio.
Teach someone in your family to say 안녕하세요 and 감사합니다 and to read their name in 한글.
Optional: send the show video for the academy's album (only with the family's written permission).
semanas.cultura: The 손하트 (finger heart) was born in Korea and today idols and athletes all over the world do it: it's the perfect gesture for the certificate photo.

evaluacion.quizzes: Every class opens with a 5-minute quiz game on the previous week (bingo, memory, 'Jay Says'). No numerical grade: each child collects stickers on their progress board and the teacher writes in the weekly note what they achieved and what's worth reviewing in the Hangul Reader.
evaluacion.tareas: Short, playful homework (≈ 20 minutes, 3 or 4 days a week, about 2 hours a week in total): a Hangul Reader drill with the exact tab, a drawing or craft, and a 10–30-second audio or video that the family sends via WhatsApp. Jay or Abby reply with a voice comment before the next class.
evaluacion.examen_final: Final show in class 8, no written exam. Three parts per child (3 minutes in total, within the 60-minute class): (1) a 30–40-second oral presentation in front of the families with greeting, name, age, family, favorite animal and food; (2) reading aloud 5 words in 한글 chosen at random from the course vocabulary; (3) 5 picture-based comprehension questions (point to the animal, food or number the teacher says).
evaluacion.oral: Continuous assessment in the workshop rooms: every week Jay or Abby record 3 indicators per child (understands the instruction in Korean, repeats with good pronunciation, produces the sentence on their own). The final show counts as the closing oral assessment; what matters is being understood and daring to speak, not grammatical perfection.
evaluacion.certificado: 'Korean for Kids (8–12) · Academia Seúl' certificate for anyone who attends at least 75% of the classes (6 out of 8; the recording does not replace attendance) and completes the final show with at least 60% of the progress-board achievements: reading their first words, introducing themselves with name and age, counting from 1 to 10, and naming animals, family members and foods. Presented on screen in class 8 and as a PDF to the family.

materiales: Academia Seúl's own materials: illustrated worksheets per session (PDF to print or view on screen), bingo cards, letter cards and the final show script template.

Hangul Reader (academiaseul.com/lector-hangul), free and with native audio: Alphabet, Learn, Practice (Vowels, Consonants, Syllables, Batchim, Words, Numbers, Pictograms, ⚡ Time Trial) and Progress tabs.
Original greeting, family and numbers songs, with lyrics in 한글 and Spanish (audio in the weekly note).
Progress sticker board (printable PDF) and weekly note to the family via WhatsApp with what we learned, what to review and a sentence to practice at home.
Home kit: white paper, colored pencils, scissors and glue; stuffed animals or animal toys (week 4) and a photo or drawing of the family (week 5).
Zoom with camera and microphone, shared whiteboard and small-group breakout rooms; recording of each class available 24 hours later to review as a family.
notas_profesor: Switch activities every 8–10 minutes and signal it with a fixed cue (a little bell or three claps with 하나, 둘, 셋): at this age, screen attention runs out fast. Always alternate screen → body → paper, and keep 2 backup games (memory and bingo) in case someone's connection drops.

Clear division of roles: Jay carries the thread of the class and the explanations in Spanish; Abby leads songs, sounds and the native pronunciation model. In breakout rooms, each teacher takes at most 6 kids and uses the same list of 3 oral indicators.

Typical pronunciation issues for Spanish speakers: ㅓ tends to come out as 'e' (it should sound like an open 'o'), ㅡ doesn't exist in Spanish (smile without rounding the lips), ㄹ between vowels is a soft 'r' and never a hard 'l', and the final ㅇ gets lost ('gan' instead of 강). Correct with modeling and games (mirror, exaggeration), never with phonetic explanations.

What to always correct: greetings with a bow, their own name pronounced well, and the sounds of the 6 vowels. What to let slide in this course: mixing up 이에요/예요, dropping 을/를, mixing 살 with Sino-Korean numbers. That gets polished in Basic 1 (A1.1) when they're older.

Differentiation by age: an 8-year-old can build syllables with cards while a 12-year-old is already reading words with batchim. Offer an 'easy' and a 'challenge' version of the same game, appoint helpers among the older kids, and let the shyest ones answer first with gestures or drawings before using their voice.

Weekly note to the family (within 24 hours after class): 3 lines max — what we learned, what to review in the Hangul Reader with the exact tab, and a sentence to practice at home. It's the main driver of retention and of homework actually getting done; always ask for a short audio or video, not written sheets.

Zoom with kids: cameras on, on-screen names written in 한글 from class 2 onward, chat for emojis only, soft music while they draw. Rehearse the final show from class 7 with a visual script (drawings instead of text), invite the families a week ahead, and confirm the October 12 date (a public holiday in Chile) from class 1 onward.
